Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the written supervisory procedures (WSP) manual for the broker-dealer distributing variable annuities and variable life; escalates unresolved gaps to the Head of Compliance

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - FINRA Rule 3110(a) supervisory system, Rule 3110(b) written procedures, Rule 2330(d) deferred variable annuity supervisory procedures and Rule 4370 BCP re-read on the FINRA Rulebook at each annual review, with the Regulatory Notice feed for the review year reconciled line by line

In-scope processes.value: Variable annuity and variable life sales supervision, principal review of new accounts and VA applications, correspondence and communications review, branch/OSJ inspections, outside business activity and private securities transaction review, complaint handling, and the annual compliance meeting

In-scope systems.value: WSP manual master and version history in the compliance evidence repository; supervisor attestations routed through the learning management system; rule-to-procedure mapping held in the Internal Regulatory System

Compliance procedure documented.value: Written Supervisory Procedures Manual with a rule-to-section map covering every FINRA rule the firm is subject to, each section naming the designated principal, the review evidence and the review frequency

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved annually by the Head of Compliance and countersigned by the CEO in the Rule 3130 certification; interim amendments approved by the designated principal for the affected section within 30 days of the triggering Regulatory Notice

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual WSP review must close before the Rule 3130 CEO certification date; the Rule 3110(a)(7) annual compliance meeting must be delivered to every registered person in the calendar year; amendments arising from a Regulatory Notice are tracked to the notice effective date

Deadline reminders configured.value: Annual review milestones at T-90 (inventory), T-60 (drafting), T-30 (legal review) against the Rule 3130 certification date, plus an alert on every FINRA Regulatory Notice with an effective date inside the next 120 days

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Every WSP edition, redline, approval and supervisor attestation retained 6 years under FINRA Rule 4511 and SEA Rule 17a-4(e)(7), the first two years in an easily accessible place

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any FINRA rule with no mapped WSP section, no named principal or no evidence artifact is raised as a supervisory-system gap with owner, due date and disposition

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off closure of every supervisory-system gap and approves the final WSP edition before it is published to supervisors

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every FINRA rule applicable to the firm on the rule-applicability inventory for the review year, plus every WSP section and every designated principal assignment in the published manual

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on coverage - any applicable FINRA rule with no WSP section, or any WSP section with no named principal, is a fail; more than 5 percent of sections missing a current-year review date makes the annual review ineffective

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Auditor must not have drafted, edited or approved any WSP section in the edition under test

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual WSP coverage test workpaper (rule inventory extract, mapping reconciliation, sampled section re-performance, exception log) filed in the compliance evidence repository under the review year

Regulator-ready documentation.value: WSP manual with effective dates, the rule-to-section map, principal designation matrix and attestation register, producible to a FINRA cycle examination request list within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Market Conduct Compliance drafts the response to FINRA Membership Application or examination requests about the supervisory system; Regulatory Counsel clears any admission of a procedural gap before it leaves the firm

checklist.step: Open the annual WSP review and build the rule-applicability inventory
actions: Open the Internal Regulatory System register, filter Regulator = FINRA and export every rule flagged applicable to the broker-dealer, with the business line and the designated principal on each row.

Ask Distribution Compliance and the Annuity Suitability team to confirm the product set for the review year (deferred variable annuities, variable life, mutual funds, 529 plans) so no rule series is dropped.
Add the rule series that apply regardless of product: 1000 registration, 2000 conduct, 3000 supervision, 4000 financial and operational, 5000 distribution.
Save the inventory as WSP-rule-inventory-<year>.xlsx in the annual review folder and record the extract date and row count on the cover sheet.
checklist.done: the inventory lists every applicable FINRA rule with business line and designated principal, dated and row-counted.

checklist.step: Map every inventoried rule to a numbered WSP section
actions: Open the current WSP manual master in the compliance evidence repository and list every numbered section with its heading.
On the inventory sheet add columns WSP section number, section heading, designated principal title, review evidence artifact and review frequency, and populate one row per rule.
Mark every rule with no matching section as UNMAPPED and every section with no rule as ORPHAN, and hand both lists to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager.
Record the mapping completion date on the cover sheet so the auditor can reconcile to the published edition.
checklist.done: each applicable rule shows a WSP section, principal, evidence artifact and frequency, with UNMAPPED and ORPHAN rows listed separately.

checklist.step: Pull the year of FINRA rule changes and score each one for WSP impact
actions: Export every FINRA Regulatory Notice and rule filing published since the last annual review from the FINRA Rule Filings and Notices pages, with notice number, subject, effective date.
Score each notice Impact = None / Text change / New section, naming the WSP section number affected and the sentence that must change.
Compare the current rulebook text of Rules 3110, 2330 and 4370 against the text quoted in the existing WSP and flag any wording that no longer matches.
Hand the scored list to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager and file it as the citation-verification evidence for the review year.
checklist.done: every notice for the year carries an impact score and, where impacting, the WSP section number and sentence to change.

checklist.step: Confirm a named principal is designated for every supervisory review
actions: Open the principal designation matrix and check every WSP section names a title, a named individual and a named alternate.

Verify each designated individual holds the required registration (Series 24 general securities principal, Series 26 investment company and variable contracts principal) by pulling their record from FINRA Gateway ahead of publication.
Ask HR for the leaver and transfer report for the year and reassign every section whose principal has left or moved, same week.
Write the reviewed matrix back into the WSP appendix with an effective date.
checklist.done: no WSP section is left without a currently registered named principal and a named alternate.

checklist.step: Rewrite the deferred variable annuity supervisory procedures under Rule 2330(d)
actions: Draft the section covering principal review of every deferred variable annuity application, stating the review must be completed before transmitting the application to the issuer and no later than 7 business days after the office of supervisory jurisdiction receives a complete application.

Write in the exchange and replacement surveillance rules under Rule 2330(b)(1)(A)(iv): comparison of surrender charges, death benefit and living benefit riders, and the 36-month prior-exchange lookback question.
Name the data source for each check - application intake in the policy administration platform, in-force values from the issuer, rep exchange rates from the surveillance report.
Circulate the draft to the New Business Case Manager and the principal reviewers for a workability read before legal review.
checklist.done: the VA section states the 7-business-day principal review, the exchange comparison fields and the 36-month lookback with named data sources.

checklist.step: Refresh the business continuity section against Rule 4370
actions: Cross-reference the WSP business continuity section to each element listed in Rule 4370(c): data back-up and recovery, mission critical systems, financial and operational assessments, alternate communications with customers and employees, alternate physical location, critical business constituent, bank and counterparty impact, regulatory reporting, and customer access to funds and securities.
Confirm the section states the annual review requirement in Rule 4370(f) and names the member of senior management who is the annual approver.
Confirm the section states the customer disclosure requirement in Rule 4370(e): disclosure at account opening, posted on the firm website and mailed on request.
Send the redline to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager with the current BCP document version number cited in the section.
checklist.done: every Rule 4370(c) element, the annual review approver and the customer disclosure route appear in the WSP section and cite the live BCP version.

checklist.step: Wire the WSP to the Rule 3120 supervisory control procedures
actions: For each WSP section, state in the supervisory controls appendix how the procedure is tested and verified, who performs the test and how often.
Confirm every producing-manager supervisory arrangement carries the Rule 3110(b)(6) heightened-supervision language and a documented rationale.
List the WSP sections whose test results feed the annual Rule 3120 report to senior management and hand the list to the report author.
File the appendix alongside the WSP master so the two versions move together.
checklist.done: every WSP section has a named test, tester and frequency in the supervisory controls appendix.

checklist.step: Run the business-line review of the draft procedures
actions: Circulate the redlined WSP sections that touch distribution to branch managers and OSJ principals with a 10-business-day comment window.
Collect comments on a single log with reviewer name, section number, comment and requested change, and reject any comment that would weaken a rule requirement rather than a process step.

Walk the three highest-volume procedures (VA application principal review, correspondence review, complaint intake) end to end with the performing team to confirm the written steps match the systems they actually use.
Return the comment log to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager with an accept or reject decision on every line.
checklist.done: every business comment is dispositioned on the log and the three highest-volume procedures are walked and confirmed executable.

checklist.step: Take the draft through legal review
actions: Read every changed section against the current FINRA rulebook text and confirm the quoted rule language and rule numbers are accurate.
Check that no section states a shorter retention or a lower standard than the rule it implements, and correct any that do.
Confirm the sections implementing Rule 2330(d) and Rule 3110(a) contain no discretion to bypass principal review.
Sign the legal review memo naming the edition number and the sections reviewed and file it in the annual review folder.
checklist.done: a dated legal review memo names the edition and confirms rule text, rule numbers and retention statements are accurate.

checklist.step: Obtain approval and cut the new WSP edition
actions: Review the change summary, the UNMAPPED and ORPHAN lists, the legal memo and the open supervisory-system gaps before signing.
Approve the edition by signing the approval page with edition number, effective date and the sections changed.
Publish the approved edition to the compliance evidence repository, lock the prior edition read-only and keep both retrievable.
Confirm the approval date falls before the Rule 3130 CEO certification date and notify the Corporate Secretary of the certification package readiness.
checklist.done: the signed edition is published with an effective date that pre-dates the Rule 3130 certification, and the prior edition is locked.

checklist.step: Push the edition to supervisors and collect attestations
actions: Load the edition summary and the changed sections into the learning management system as an assigned item for every registered principal and branch manager, with a 30-day completion window.
Set the attestation wording to name the edition number and require confirmation that the individual has read the sections for which they are the designated principal.
Run the completion report weekly and send the outstanding list to each supervisor's manager at day 15 and day 25.
Export the completed attestation register to the compliance evidence repository at day 31.
checklist.done: every designated principal has an attestation against the named edition, or is on an escalated outstanding list.

checklist.step: Deliver the Rule 3110(a)(7) annual compliance meeting
actions: Build the agenda from the WSP changes of the year, the Firm Element needs analysis findings and the exam and complaint themes supplied by Market Conduct Compliance.
Schedule delivery so every registered person and every registered principal attends at least once in the calendar year, using live sessions plus a recorded make-up path with a knowledge check.
Record attendance per person with date, delivery method and the interactive element used, and chase non-attendees at 30 and 15 days before year end.
File the agenda, materials and attendance register in the compliance evidence repository as the Rule 3110(a)(7) evidence.
checklist.done: every registered person has a dated attendance record for the calendar year and the agenda and materials are filed.

checklist.step: Reconcile branch and OSJ registrations to the supervisor assignments
actions: Pull the firm branch office list from FINRA Gateway (Form BR records) and compare it to the WSP principal designation matrix.
Confirm every OSJ has an on-site principal and every non-OSJ branch is assigned to a supervising OSJ named in the matrix.
File a Form BR amendment through FINRA Gateway within 30 days for any office whose supervisor, address or activity has changed.
Record the reconciliation date and the amendments filed in the annual review folder.
checklist.done: the branch list and the designation matrix agree, with any Form BR amendment filed within 30 days of the change.

checklist.step: Log every unclosed gap as a supervisory-system exception
actions: Raise one issue per UNMAPPED rule, unassigned principal, unrefreshed section and missing attestation, quoting the rule number and the WSP section.
Assign a root cause (rule change missed, reorganisation, product launch without a procedure) and a named owner at manager level or above.
Set the remediation date inside 90 days and require an interim compensating control statement for anything longer.
Report the open list to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting with age and owner.
checklist.done: every gap has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a committee reporting entry.

checklist.step: Retain the edition and its supporting record under Rule 4511
actions: Move the edition, redlines, comment log, legal memo, approval page and attestation register into the document management repository under WSP / <year>.
Apply the 6-year retention label required by FINRA Rule 4511 and SEA Rule 17a-4(e)(7), with the first two years in the readily accessible tier.
Confirm the record is indexed and searchable by edition number, effective date, rule number and section number.
Confirm the write-once storage or audit-trail attribute is applied so editions cannot be silently overwritten.
checklist.done: the edition record is filed, labelled for 6-year retention, searchable by rule and section, and protected from overwrite.

testing.step: Build the population of applicable rules and published WSP sections
actions: Extract from the Internal Regulatory System every FINRA rule flagged applicable to the broker-dealer as at the review-year end, with business line and designated principal.
Extract the section list from the published WSP edition in the compliance evidence repository and record the edition number and effective date.
Compare both extracts to the prior-year population and explain every added and removed rule with reference to a Regulatory Notice or a product change.
Sign the population sheet as complete before any sampling begins.
testing.done: the rule population and the WSP section list are extracted, reconciled year on year and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the rule population to the rule-to-section map
actions: Join the rule population to the mapping sheet on rule number and list every rule with no WSP section and every section with no rule.
Independently confirm the applicability of five rules the firm marked not applicable, reading the rule scope text on the FINRA rulebook.
Confirm every mapped row carries a designated principal, an evidence artifact and a review frequency, and list blanks as exceptions.
Record the coverage percentage and the unmapped count in the workpaper.
testing.done: coverage is quantified and every unmapped rule, orphan section and blank field is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw the section sample and document the method
actions: Take 100 percent of the sections implementing Rules 3110, 2330 and 4370 and 100 percent of sections changed during the review year.
Take 20 further sections by seeded random selection from the remaining published sections.
Record the seed, the population size, the selection date and the selector name so the sample can be redrawn.
Confirm no sampled section was drafted or approved by anyone on the test team.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all changed sections plus the three key rules, and is free of self-review.

testing.step: Re-perform the citation check against the live FINRA rulebook
actions: For each sampled section, open the cited rule on the FINRA rulebook and read the current text without looking at the WSP first.
Compare the rule requirement to the WSP wording and mark any section that states a weaker standard, a longer deadline or a superseded rule number.
Confirm the Rule 2330(d) section still states the 7-business-day principal review window and the Rule 4370 section still lists all nine Rule 4370(c) elements.
Capture the rulebook page for each sampled section into the workpaper with the retrieval date.
testing.done: each sampled section has an independent citation re-performance note and a dated rulebook capture.

testing.step: Verify the designated principals are real, registered and current
actions: For every sampled section, take the named principal and pull their registration record from FINRA Gateway.
Confirm the individual holds the principal registration the role requires (Series 24 or Series 26 as applicable) and is still an active associated person of the firm.
Confirm a named alternate exists and is separately registered.
Flag as an exception any section naming a leaver, a title with no individual, or an unregistered person.
testing.done: every sampled section names a currently registered principal and alternate, or the gap is logged.

testing.step: Trace the sampled procedures to evidence they were actually operated
actions: For each sampled section, request the evidence artifact the WSP names (principal review queue export, correspondence review log, branch inspection report, complaint file) for one month of the review year.
Confirm the artifact exists, is dated inside the review year and shows the reviewer and the review date the section requires.
Where the named artifact does not exist, record a fail - a procedure with no output is not a supervisory system.
Reference the artifact identifiers in the workpaper so the evidence can be re-pulled.
testing.done: each sampled section is traced to a dated, attributable evidence artifact or recorded as a fail.

testing.step: Test the change control from Regulatory Notice to published amendment
actions: Take 10 Regulatory Notices scored Text change or New section during the review year.
Trace each to the WSP redline, the approval page and the published edition, and compare the publication date to the notice effective date.
Recompute the lag in calendar days and list every amendment published after the rule effective date.
Confirm the compensating control stated for any late amendment was actually in place during the lag.
testing.done: each sampled notice traces to a published amendment with a computed lag and any late publication is listed.

testing.step: Test attestation and annual compliance meeting completeness
actions: Take the registered person roster from FINRA Gateway as at year end and join it to the learning management system attestation and annual compliance meeting completion reports.
Compute the completion percentage for the WSP attestation and for the Rule 3110(a)(7) meeting, separately for registered persons and for principals.
Sample 15 completions and confirm the record shows the individual, the edition or session, the date and the delivery method.
List every registered person with no meeting attendance in the calendar year as an exception.
testing.done: completion rates are computed off the FINRA roster and every non-attending registered person is listed.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception quoting the rule number, the WSP section and what was missing.
Assign a root cause (notice not triaged, principal departure, product launched without a procedure, evidence never produced) and an owner at manager level or above.
Set a remediation date and, for any section with no operating evidence, require a look-back over the affected period before closure.
Carry every open exception into next year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception carries an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the annual WSP test
actions: Compare the coverage result to the thresholds: zero unmapped applicable rules, zero sections without a named principal, no more than 5 percent of sections lacking a current-year review date.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper references behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who drafted and approved no sampled section, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the Compliance Committee and the CEO ahead of the Rule 3130 certification and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion, the coverage percentages and the date reported to the Committee and the CEO.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the annual Market Conduct Annual Statement submission for the life and annuity lines and the annual Firm Element needs analysis data feed that supports it

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - the NAIC MCAS Data Call and Definitions for the life and annuity lines for the data year, plus FINRA Rule 1240(b) Firm Element and Rule 3110(a)(7) annual compliance meeting, re-read at the start of each filing cycle

In-scope processes.value: Annual MCAS data extraction, validation and submission for every participating state where the writing company exceeded the premium threshold, and the annual Firm Element needs analysis, written training plan and delivery for registered persons selling variable annuities

In-scope systems.value: NAIC iSite+ / MCAS application for submission and validation; source data from the policy administration platform and claims platform; Firm Element delivery and completion records in the learning management system

Compliance procedure documented.value: MCAS Filing Procedure - participation determination by state and line, data element mapping to the NAIC Data Call definitions, validation and variance review, attestation and submission; plus the Firm Element Needs Analysis and Training Plan procedure

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance with the Regulatory Reporting Manager as data owner; re-approved each year after the NAIC publishes the updated Data Call and Definitions

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: MCAS data year ends 31 December and the submission is due by 30 April in the following year for the life and annuity lines, with state-specific variations tracked per jurisdiction; the Firm Element needs analysis and written training plan must be completed and delivery evidenced within the same calendar year

Deadline reminders configured.value: Filing calendar alerts at 1 February (extract ready), 15 March (validation clean), 15 April (attestation signed) and 25 April (submitted) against the 30 April deadline, one track per state

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: MCAS submission confirmations, the submitted data files, validation reports, variance explanations and the Firm Element needs analysis and completion registers retained 6 years under FINRA Rule 4511 and per state record retention rules

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any missed state, late submission, failed validation left unresolved or post-submission data correction is logged with root cause, the corrected resubmission date and the state notification made

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every late or amended MCAS submission and every Firm Element delivery shortfall before the exception is closed

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every state and line combination where a writing company met the MCAS participation threshold for the data year, plus every registered person covered by the Firm Element plan for that year

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero missed states and zero late submissions; any MCAS data element varying more than 10 percent from the prior year without a documented explanation is a fail; Firm Element delivery below 100 percent of covered persons by 31 December is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual; the test runs once after the 30 April submission window closes, with an interim readiness check in February on the extract and participation list

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have prepared, validated or submitted any MCAS file in the data year

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual MCAS and Firm Element test workpaper (participation determination, source-to-submission reconciliation, sampled data element re-performance, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: MCAS submission confirmations by state with timestamps, the submitted data files, the reconciliation to the policy and claims systems, and the Firm Element needs analysis, plan and completion register, producible to a state market conduct examiner or a FINRA examiner within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Reporting answers state MCAS data queries through the NAIC MCAS application messaging; Market Conduct Compliance owns any resulting state market conduct inquiry and Regulatory Counsel clears responses that concede a data error

checklist.step: Read the new MCAS Data Call and Definitions and log every change
actions: Download the NAIC MCAS Data Call and Definitions for the life and the annuity lines for the data year from NAIC iSite+ as soon as it is published.
Diff the element list against the prior year and record every added, removed and redefined element, quoting the new definition text.
Route redefined elements to the Data Steward and the source system owners with the mapping change required in each.
Circulate the change log to Market Conduct Compliance and the Statutory Reporting Manager and file it in the filing folder for the data year.
checklist.done: the element change log for the data year is written, sourced from the published Data Call, and issued to every source system owner.

checklist.step: Determine which states and lines the company must file
actions: Pull direct written premium by state, by line and by NAIC company code for the data year from the general ledger and the statutory reporting pack.
Compare each state total against that state's MCAS participation threshold in the Data Call and mark FILE or BELOW THRESHOLD with the tested premium value on the row.
Check the NAIC participating states list for states newly adopting MCAS for annuities and add them to the file list.
Have the Statutory Reporting Manager confirm the premium figures agree to the filed annual statement state page before the list is frozen.
checklist.done: every state and line carries a FILE or BELOW THRESHOLD decision with the tested premium value agreed to the annual statement state page.

checklist.step: Confirm company registration and user access in the NAIC MCAS application
actions: Log in to NAIC iSite+ and open the MCAS application, confirming each writing company appears under the correct NAIC company code and group code.
Register the company for each state and line on the FILE list before the filing window opens.
Confirm the submitter and the attester user roles are assigned to current employees and remove leavers.
Record the registration confirmations and the user list in the filing folder.
checklist.done: every FILE state and line is registered in the MCAS application with current submitter and attester users.

checklist.step: Extract the policy administration data for the MCAS elements
actions: Run the MCAS extract against the policy administration platform for policies in force at any time in the data year, keyed by state of issue and line.

Populate the policy-side elements the Data Call defines: policies in force at year end, policies issued, applications received, applications declined, replacements, surrenders and free-look cancellations.
Apply the definition change log so redefined elements use the new rule, and record which elements changed logic this year.
Deliver the extract with row counts by state to the Regulatory Reporting Analyst and keep the query version in the source code repository.
checklist.done: the policy-side extract is produced per the current definitions, row-counted by state, with the query version retained.

checklist.step: Extract the claims and complaint data for the MCAS elements
actions: Run the claims extract for claims received, paid, denied and closed without payment in the data year, with the days-to-payment buckets the Data Call requires.

Pull the complaint counts from the complaint register, splitting complaints received directly from consumers and complaints received via a department of insurance, and reconcile the DOI count to the NAIC Complaints Database records for the company.
Compute the lawsuit counts opened and closed in the period from the legal matter management system.
Hand the extracts, with definitions applied and counts by state, to the Regulatory Reporting Analyst.
checklist.done: claims, complaint and lawsuit elements are extracted per definition, with the DOI complaint count reconciled to the NAIC complaints data.

checklist.step: Reconcile the extracts to the source systems before loading
actions: Reconcile policies in force by state to the in-force listing used for the statutory annual statement and explain every difference over 0.5 percent.
Reconcile claims paid counts and amounts to the claims paid register and to the general ledger claims expense by state.
Tie the complaint counts to the complaint register totals and to the counts reported to each state department of insurance.
Sign the reconciliation sheet and store it beside the extract files in the filing folder.
checklist.done: each MCAS element group is tied to its source of record with every material difference explained and the sheet signed.

checklist.step: Load the file and clear every NAIC validation message
actions: Format the data to the NAIC MCAS template for the line and upload it in the MCAS application under the correct company, state, line and data year.
Work the validation report top to bottom, resolving every hard error by correcting the data at source rather than in the file.
For each soft warning, write the explanation into the comment field, naming the business reason (product launch, block reinsured, system conversion).
Re-upload until the validation report is clean of hard errors and save the final validation report to the filing folder.
checklist.done: the upload passes with zero hard errors and every soft warning carries a written business explanation.

checklist.step: Run the year-on-year variance review before attestation
actions: Build the state-by-state comparison of every element against the prior two data years and flag any element moving more than 10 percent.
Ask the owning function for a written cause on each flagged element - Claims for payment timeliness moves, Distribution for replacement and surrender moves, Consumer Affairs for complaint moves.
Compare the resulting complaint and replacement ratios to the industry benchmark ranges the NAIC publishes and note where the company sits as an outlier.
Attach the variance pack to the attestation request so the attester signs with the outliers in front of them.
checklist.done: every element moving more than 10 percent has a written cause and the outlier position against the NAIC benchmarks is documented.

checklist.step: Obtain the officer attestation and submit each state filing
actions: Route the completed data, validation report and variance pack to the attesting officer for signature, targeting 15 April.
Submit each state and line in the MCAS application before 30 April and capture the submission confirmation with its timestamp and confirmation number.
Record the confirmation number, state, line, company code and submission timestamp on the filing tracker row for each state.
Where a state grants an extension, obtain it in writing from that state before the deadline and file it with the tracker row.
checklist.done: every FILE state shows a timestamped submission confirmation on or before 30 April, or a written extension.

checklist.step: Answer state follow-up questions and manage any resubmission
actions: Monitor the MCAS application messaging and the regulatory mailbox for state data queries and log each with the state, question, received date and a 10-business-day internal response target.
Trace each query back to the source extract and answer with the reconciled figure and the definition applied.
Where a data error is confirmed, prepare the corrected file, obtain a fresh attestation and resubmit in the MCAS application, noting the correction in the comment field.
Notify Market Conduct Compliance of any correction that changes a ratio the state monitors.
checklist.done: every state query is answered inside the internal target and every confirmed error is resubmitted with a fresh attestation.

checklist.step: Run the annual Firm Element needs analysis
actions: Assemble the inputs the analysis must consider: the product mix sold in the year (deferred variable annuities, variable life), customer complaints, exam and internal audit findings, Rule 4530 disclosures and the year's Regulatory Notices.
Identify the covered registered persons - registered representatives with public customer contact and their immediate supervisors - from the FINRA Gateway roster.
Write the needs analysis document naming the training needs found, the population affected and the evidence behind each need.
Have the Head of Compliance approve the needs analysis before the training plan is written.
checklist.done: a dated, approved needs analysis names the covered population and each identified training need with its evidence.

checklist.step: Write the Firm Element training plan for the year
actions: Turn each identified need into a module with learning objectives, the covered population, the delivery method and the completion deadline.
Include the product-specific content Rule 1240(b) expects for variable annuities: features and riders, surrender charges, tax treatment, exchange and replacement suitability under Rule 2330.
Load the plan into the learning management system, assign the modules to the covered population and set the completion deadline at 30 November to leave chase time.
File the signed plan in the compliance evidence repository as the Rule 1240(b) written training plan for the year.
checklist.done: a written, signed training plan maps every identified need to an assigned module with a population and a deadline.

checklist.step: Deliver the training and chase completion to 100 percent
actions: Launch the assigned modules and run the completion report weekly, split by branch and by supervisor.
Escalate outstanding names to the branch OSJ principal at 30 days and to the Head of Compliance at 15 days before the deadline.
For anyone still outstanding after the deadline, apply the heightened step stated in the WSP - restrict new business until the module is completed.
Export the completion register with person, module, completion date and score to the compliance evidence repository at year end.
checklist.done: the completion register shows every covered person complete, or under a documented business restriction.

checklist.step: Log filing and training exceptions
actions: Raise an issue for every missed state, late submission, unexplained validation warning, post-submission correction and incomplete Firm Element assignment.
Assign a root cause (participation threshold missed, source system change, definition change not implemented, roster out of date) and a named owner.
Set a remediation date before the next data year extract begins so the fix is proven before the next cycle.
Report open items to the Compliance Committee with the state and the deadline missed.
checklist.done: every filing and training exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner and a pre-next-cycle remediation date.

checklist.step: Archive the submission record for the data year
actions: File the submitted data files, validation reports, reconciliation sheets, variance pack, attestations and submission confirmations under MCAS / <data year> / <state>.
File the Firm Element needs analysis, training plan and completion register in the same data-year folder.
Apply the 6-year retention label required by FINRA Rule 4511 and confirm the state retention requirement for each filed state is met or exceeded.
Confirm the archive is searchable by data year, state, NAIC company code and confirmation number.
checklist.done: the full data-year record is archived, retention-labelled and searchable by state and confirmation number.

testing.step: Rebuild the population of states the company was required to file
actions: Take direct written premium by state, line and NAIC company code from the filed statutory annual statement state pages for the data year.
Apply each state's published MCAS participation threshold independently and produce your own FILE list.
Compare your list to the company's participation determination and list every state the company excluded that your test includes.
Sign the population as complete before sampling.
testing.done: an independently derived FILE list exists and every difference to the company list is itemised.

testing.step: Confirm every required state was actually submitted and on time
actions: In the MCAS application, open the submission history for each company code and export state, line, data year, confirmation number and submission timestamp.
Match every state on the independent FILE list to a submission confirmation and list unmatched states as automatic fails.
Compare each submission timestamp to 30 April and to any written extension held on file, and compute the days late.
Capture the submission history screen into the workpaper.
testing.done: every required state traces to a timestamped confirmation, with days late computed and unmatched states failed.

testing.step: Draw the data element sample and record the method
actions: Take 100 percent of the elements flagged in the variance review and 100 percent of elements whose definition changed for the data year.
Take 15 further state and element combinations by seeded random selection from the submitted files.
Record the seed, population size, selection date and selector so the sample can be redrawn.
Confirm no sampled element was prepared or validated by a member of the test team.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers changed and flagged elements, and is free of self-review.

testing.step: Re-perform the element calculation from the source systems
actions: Read the NAIC definition for each sampled element and write your own extraction logic before looking at the company query.
Run it against the policy administration platform and the claims platform for the sampled state and compare your count to the submitted value.
Investigate every difference over 1 percent and classify it as definition interpretation, data quality or extraction error.
Record both figures, the difference and the classification in the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled element has an independently recomputed value, a stated difference and a classification of any gap.

testing.step: Trace the complaint elements to the complaint register and DOI records
actions: Pull the complaint register for the data year and count complaints received directly and via a department of insurance, by state.
Compare both counts to the submitted MCAS values and to the NAIC Complaints Database records for the company codes.
Sample 10 complaint files and confirm the receipt date, state and channel recorded in the register match the file itself.
List any complaint captured in the DOI record but absent from the register as a completeness failure.
testing.done: complaint counts reconcile across register, MCAS submission and the NAIC complaints data, or the gap is itemised.

testing.step: Recompute the deadline and attestation controls
actions: For each submitted state, confirm the attestation is signed by the named officer and dated on or before the submission timestamp.
Confirm any resubmission carries a fresh attestation dated on or before the resubmission timestamp.
Recompute the internal milestone dates (1 February, 15 March, 15 April) against the actual completion dates recorded on the filing tracker and note slippage.
Flag any submission made without a signed attestation as a reportable control failure.
testing.done: every submission and resubmission is covered by a pre-dated officer attestation and milestone slippage is quantified.

testing.step: Test the Firm Element needs analysis for substance
actions: Read the needs analysis and confirm it cites the year's actual complaints, exam findings, Rule 4530 disclosures and product mix rather than generic statements.
Confirm the covered population was derived from the FINRA Gateway registered person roster and includes supervisors of persons with public customer contact.
Trace three identified needs through to modules in the training plan and confirm the module content addresses the need.
Confirm the analysis and plan are dated inside the calendar year they cover.
testing.done: the needs analysis is evidenced by named year-specific inputs and each sampled need traces to a delivered module.

testing.step: Test Firm Element delivery against the registered person roster
actions: Take the registered person roster from FINRA Gateway as at 31 December and join it to the learning management system completion register.
Compute the completion percentage and list every covered person with an incomplete assignment at year end.
Sample 15 completion records and confirm each shows the person, module, completion date and assessment result.
Confirm the documented business restriction was actually applied to anyone completing after the deadline.
testing.done: completion is measured against the FINRA roster and every incomplete person is listed with the restriction evidence checked.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the state, line, element or person and the amount or count in error.
Assign a root cause (threshold misapplied, definition change not built, source reconciliation skipped, roster stale) and an owner at manager level or above.
Set the remediation date before the next data year extract and require evidence of the corrected query or process.
Carry every open exception into next year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception carries an issue, a root cause, an owner, a pre-next-cycle remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the MCAS and Firm Element test
actions: Compare results to the thresholds: zero missed states, zero late submissions, no unexplained element variance over 10 percent, 100 percent Firm Element completion.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper references behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared and validated no MCAS file, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Compliance Committee and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under the data year.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion, the missed-state and late-filing counts and the Firm Element completion rate.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the quarterly conduct metrics pack for the broker-dealer - complaint rates, variable annuity exchange and replacement rates, Rule 4530 reporting timeliness, Rule 2210 communications filing turnaround and Rule 2330 principal review timeliness

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Every red breach must have a documented action inside 30 days - any unactioned red is a fail; any metric whose recomputed value differs from the reported value by more than 2 percent is a fail; any Rule 4530 event filed after 30 calendar days is a reportable breach, not a test exception

checklist.step: Agree the metric definitions and thresholds for the quarter
actions: Open the metric register and confirm each metric has a written numerator, denominator, population filter, source system and owner.

Set the red and amber thresholds for the quarter using the prior four quarters of firm data and the industry benchmark ranges published in the current FINRA Report on Examination and Risk Monitoring Program.
Route any threshold change to the Head of Compliance for approval before the quarter is calculated, never after the numbers are seen.
Publish the approved register to the dashboard team and file the approval in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: every metric has an approved definition and a red and amber threshold set before the quarter is calculated.

checklist.step: Extract the variable annuity transaction population for the quarter
actions: Extract from the policy administration platform every deferred variable annuity application received, issued, surrendered and exchanged with a transaction date inside the quarter, keyed by writing company, state and selling registered representative CRD number.
Add the fields the exchange metrics need: source contract carrier, surrender charge amount and remaining surrender period, prior exchange date within the last 36 months, and rider elections.
Add the variable life policies issued and lapsed in the quarter on the same key so both product families are measured.
Deliver the extract with row counts by branch to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager and store the query version in the source code repository.
checklist.done: the quarter transaction extract is produced by representative CRD with the exchange fields populated and row-counted by branch.

checklist.step: Extract the complaint population and classify it
actions: Extract every written customer complaint received in the quarter from the complaint case management tool with received date, product, representative CRD, branch, allegation category and status.
Confirm the Rule 4513 complaint register fields are complete on each record: complainant name, date received, and the disposition.
Split the population by channel - direct to firm, via a state department of insurance, via FINRA - so the regulator-sourced rate can be measured separately.
Hand the classified extract to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager with a signed completeness statement.
checklist.done: the quarter complaint population is extracted with Rule 4513 fields complete, classified by allegation and channel.

checklist.step: Pull the Rule 2330 principal review timeliness data
actions: For every deferred variable annuity application in the quarter, extract the date the office of supervisory jurisdiction received a complete application and the date the principal approved or rejected it.
Compute elapsed business days and flag every application reviewed beyond the 7 business day window in FINRA Rule 2330(c).
Split the results by principal and by branch so a single overloaded reviewer is visible.
Send the flagged list to the branch OSJ principals with a request for a written cause on each item.
checklist.done: principal review elapsed days are computed per application and every breach of the 7 business day window is listed by principal.

checklist.step: Pull the Rule 2210 and 2211 communications metrics
actions: Extract every retail communication concerning variable annuities and variable life used in the quarter, with first use date, principal approval date and the FINRA Advertising Regulation filing date where filing was required.
Compute the days from first use to filing and flag anything filed beyond the 10 business day window, and flag anything used with no pre-use principal approval.

Log the content standard failures found in review under Rule 2210(d)(1) - unwarranted claims, omitted material risks, missing fee and surrender charge disclosure - and the Rule 2211 requirements specific to variable products.
Report the counts and the individual items to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager.
checklist.done: communications counts, filing lags and content standard failures are produced with the individual items identified.

checklist.step: Pull the Rule 4530 reporting timeliness data
actions: Extract every Rule 4530 candidate event opened in the quarter with the date the firm knew or had reason to know, the event category, and the FINRA Gateway filing date.
Compute elapsed calendar days and flag every event filed beyond 30 calendar days and every event still open past day 20.
Add the quarterly statistical complaint filing under Rule 4530(d) and confirm it was made within 15 calendar days after the end of the calendar quarter.
Escalate any event past the deadline to Regulatory Counsel the same day it is identified.
checklist.done: every Rule 4530 event has an elapsed-day calculation, late filings are escalated and the quarterly statistical filing date is recorded.

checklist.step: Calculate the metrics and refresh the dashboard
actions: Load the extracts into the enterprise data warehouse and run the approved metric definitions to produce firm, branch and representative level values.

Compute the core rates: complaints per 1000 policies in force, exchange rate as a percentage of VA sales, surrender-inside-surrender-charge rate, principal review breach rate, communications filing breach rate, Firm Element completion rate.
Publish the dashboard with a data-as-at date, the source extract row counts and a visible definition tooltip on each metric.
Notify the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager that the quarter is refreshed within 5 business days of quarter end.
checklist.done: the dashboard shows every approved metric at firm, branch and representative level with a stated data-as-at date and row counts.

checklist.step: Reconcile the dashboard back to the source systems
actions: Tie policies in force and VA sales counts on the dashboard to the policy administration platform totals for the quarter and explain any difference over 0.5 percent.
Tie the complaint count to the Rule 4513 complaint register total and to the count reported in the Rule 4530(d) quarterly statistical filing.
Tie the Firm Element completion rate denominator to the FINRA Gateway registered person roster as at quarter end.
Sign the reconciliation and attach it to the quarter pack so the numbers are defensible before they are discussed.
checklist.done: each headline metric is tied to its source of record with differences explained and the reconciliation signed.

checklist.step: Compare the results to the regulatory benchmarks
actions: Place each firm-level metric against the approved threshold and against the industry position - NAIC complaint index for the writing companies and the themes in the current FINRA exam findings report.
Mark each metric green, amber or red and write a one-paragraph cause for every amber and red, sourced from the owning function.
Rank branches and representatives by composite outlier score and produce the top 20 list for supervisory action.
Circulate the draft pack to the Head of Compliance and the Distribution Operations Manager before it is finalised.
checklist.done: every metric is rated against threshold and benchmark, with a sourced cause on each amber and red and a ranked outlier list.

checklist.step: Trigger the supervisory action each red breach requires
actions: For every representative on the red list, open a for-cause review of their quarter transactions and complaints and record the finding on the representative file.
Apply the action the procedure states: heightened supervision plan with named supervising principal, pre-approval of VA applications, targeted training assignment, or restriction on new business.
For every branch on the red list, schedule an unannounced branch inspection under FINRA Rule 3110(c) within the following quarter.
Record each action with owner and due date and confirm the affected supervisor has acknowledged it in writing.
checklist.done: every red representative and branch has a named action, a named supervising principal and a written acknowledgement.

checklist.step: Feed the outlier findings into the Firm Element needs analysis
actions: Summarise the quarter's recurring conduct themes - exchange suitability, disclosure of surrender charges, rider fee explanations - and hand them to the Firm Element needs analysis owner.
Assign targeted modules in the learning management system to the affected representatives with a 30-day completion deadline.
Track completion weekly and escalate non-completion to the branch OSJ principal.
Record the theme, the module assigned and the completion evidence on the representative file.
checklist.done: each recurring theme is written into the needs analysis input and targeted modules are assigned and tracked to completion.

checklist.step: Present the pack to the Compliance Committee
actions: Issue the pack within 30 calendar days of quarter end with the metric table, trend charts, benchmark position, red list and open actions.
Take decisions on any metric red for two consecutive quarters - product or channel level intervention rather than individual supervision.
Record the decisions, owners and dates in the minutes and load the pack to the board portal.
Confirm the pack is referenced in the annual Rule 3120 supervisory control report to senior management.
checklist.done: the pack is issued inside 30 days, minuted with owned decisions, and linked to the Rule 3120 report.

checklist.step: Recalibrate the thresholds after the fourth quarter
actions: After the fourth quarter, rebuild the four-quarter distribution for each metric and propose new red and amber thresholds by 31 December.
Compare the proposed thresholds to the current FINRA exam findings themes and to the NAIC complaint index position for each writing company.
Present the changes with the count of representatives who would newly breach at the proposed level so the operational load is visible.
Obtain Head of Compliance approval and version the metric register before the first quarter of the new year is calculated.
checklist.done: new thresholds are approved and versioned by 31 December with the breach-population impact stated.

checklist.step: Log unresolved breaches as compliance exceptions
actions: Raise an issue for every red breach with no action inside 30 days, every late Rule 4530 filing and every communication used without principal approval.
Assign a root cause (supervisory capacity, definition ambiguity, source data gap, representative conduct) and an owner at manager level or above.
Set a remediation date inside the following quarter and require the action evidence to be attached at closure.
Report the open list with age to the Compliance Committee each quarter.
checklist.done: every unresolved breach has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and committee visibility.

checklist.step: Archive the quarter pack and its supporting extracts
actions: File the pack, the source extracts, the reconciliation, the breach action log and the committee minutes under Conduct metrics / <year> / <quarter>.
Apply the 6-year FINRA Rule 4511 retention label, and the 4-year Rule 4513 label on the complaint register extract with the first two years readily accessible.
Confirm the archive is searchable by quarter, metric, branch and representative CRD number.
Confirm the dashboard snapshot is stored as a fixed file so the reported numbers cannot change after the fact.
checklist.done: the quarter record is archived with a frozen dashboard snapshot, retention labels applied and CRD-level searchability.

testing.step: Rebuild the quarter population independently
actions: Extract all VA and variable life transactions, complaints, retail communications and Rule 4530 events with a quarter date directly from the policy administration platform, the complaint case management tool and the GRC platform.
Compare your row counts to the row counts stated on the quarter pack and investigate every difference.
Confirm the population is keyed to the FINRA Gateway registered person roster so no active representative is missing from the denominator.
Sign the population sheet as complete before sampling.
testing.done: an independently extracted population is reconciled to the pack row counts and to the registered person roster.

testing.step: Reconcile the reported metric values to the source of record
actions: For each headline metric, trace the numerator and denominator on the pack back to the warehouse tables and then to the source system totals.
Recompute the complaint rate per 1000 policies in force and the VA exchange rate from your own population.
List every metric where your recomputed value differs from the reported value by more than 2 percent as a fail.
Record both values and the difference in the workpaper.
testing.done: every headline metric is recomputed from source and differences over 2 percent are recorded as fails.

testing.step: Draw the sample of breaches and transactions
actions: Take 100 percent of red threshold breaches and 100 percent of Rule 4530 events in the quarter.
Take 25 VA transactions and 15 complaint files by seeded random selection from the remaining population.
Record the seed, population size, selection date and selector so the sample can be redrawn.
Confirm no sampled item was calculated or dispositioned by a member of the test team.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all red breaches and Rule 4530 events, and is free of self-review.

testing.step: Re-perform the threshold judgement on the sampled metrics
actions: Take the approved metric register as it stood at the start of the quarter and apply the thresholds yourself to the recomputed values.
Compare your red, amber and green ratings to the ratings on the pack and treat any softened rating as an exception.
Confirm no threshold was changed after the quarter data was visible by comparing the register version date to the dashboard refresh date.
Capture the register version and the rating comparison in the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled metric has an independent rating, and any post-hoc threshold change or softened rating is logged.

testing.step: Trace every red breach to a real supervisory action
actions: For each red representative or branch, open the breach record and read the action taken, the named supervising principal and the written acknowledgement.
Trace the action to its operational evidence - the heightened supervision plan, the pre-approval queue entries, the branch inspection report, the training completion record.
Compute the days from pack issue to action start and list anything beyond 30 days.
Treat a breach with a recorded action but no operational evidence as a fail.
testing.done: every red breach traces to a dated action with operational evidence, or is recorded as a fail.

testing.step: Recompute the Rule 2330 and Rule 2210 deadline maths
actions: For 20 sampled VA applications, recompute business days from OSJ receipt of a complete application to principal decision and compare to the 7 business day requirement.
For 10 sampled retail communications, recompute business days from first use to the FINRA Advertising Regulation filing date against the 10 business day requirement.
For every Rule 4530 event, recompute calendar days from the knowledge date to the FINRA Gateway filing date against the 30 calendar day requirement.
List every recomputed breach that the pack did not report.
testing.done: all three deadline calculations are independently recomputed and unreported breaches are itemised.

testing.step: Test the complaint register for completeness against Rule 4513
actions: Search the customer correspondence mailbox and the contact centre case log for the quarter for items meeting the written complaint definition and check each appears on the register.
For 15 sampled register entries confirm the record holds complainant identity, receipt date, the nature of the complaint and the disposition.
Compare the register to the complaints reported in the Rule 4530(d) quarterly statistical filing and to any state department of insurance complaint notices received.
List every complaint present in a source but absent from the register as a completeness failure.
testing.done: the register is proven complete against correspondence, contact centre, Rule 4530(d) and state notices, or gaps are itemised.

testing.step: Verify the pack was issued and governed on time
actions: Compare the pack issue date to quarter end plus 30 calendar days and record any slippage.
Read the Compliance Committee minutes and confirm the pack was tabled, the red list discussed and decisions recorded with owners and dates.
Confirm any metric red for two consecutive quarters carries a product or channel level decision rather than another individual action.
Capture the minute reference into the workpaper.
testing.done: issue timeliness is measured and every repeated red is shown to carry an escalated, minuted decision.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the metric, the representative or branch, and the measured versus reported value.
Assign a root cause (definition drift, source data gap, supervisory capacity, threshold set after the fact) and an owner at manager level or above.
Set a remediation date inside the next quarter and require the corrected query or the completed supervisory action as closure evidence.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception carries an issue, a root cause, an owner, a next-quarter remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the quarterly conduct metrics test
actions: Compare results to the thresholds: zero unactioned red breaches, no recomputation difference over 2 percent, zero late Rule 4530 filings.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper references behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who built and presented none of the pack, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under the quarter.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion, the recomputation differences and the unactioned breach count.
