checklist.step: Build the binder index from the FINRA cycle exam request list
actions: Take the most recent FINRA cycle examination request list and the firm's prior exam request lists and list every document category they asked for.

Create one binder section per category - organisation and registration, WSPs, supervisory designations, branch inspections, complaints, communications, VA suitability, best execution, AML, code of conduct and attestations, personal trading, gifts, outside activities, BCP, financial and operational records.
Assign each section a named owner, a refresh frequency and the exact evidence artifact expected, and store the index at the root of the exam binder.
Have the Head of Compliance and the General Counsel approve the index before it is published to owners.
checklist.done: the binder index covers every category on the FINRA request list with an owner, a refresh frequency and a named artifact per section.

checklist.step: Refresh the firm profile and registration section
actions: Pull the current Form BD, the membership agreement and any Rule 1017 continuing membership application approvals from FINRA Gateway.
Pull the branch office list (Form BR records) and the registered person roster with registration categories and dates.
Confirm the organisational chart, ownership chart and affiliate list match the Form BD schedules and correct any drift with the Corporate Secretary.
File the refreshed set in the binder section with the retrieval date on each document.
checklist.done: the registration section holds a current Form BD, branch list, roster and organisation chart, each dated at retrieval.

checklist.step: Issue and version the code of conduct
actions: Review the code against FINRA Rule 2010 standards of commercial honor and confirm it addresses conflicts of interest, personal trading, gifts and entertainment, outside business activities, and the duty and route to escalate concerns.
Add or update the escalation and anti-retaliation section naming the reporting channels, including the anonymous channel and the Ethics Officer as owner.
Route the draft to the General Counsel and the Head of Compliance for approval and cut a numbered edition with an effective date.
Publish the edition to the binder section and lock the prior edition read-only.
checklist.done: a numbered, approved code edition covering conflicts, personal trading, gifts, outside activities and escalation is published and dated.

checklist.step: Run the periodic code of conduct attestation campaign
actions: Assign the code attestation in the learning management system to every associated person on the FINRA Gateway roster, opening 1 October and closing 31 December.

Write the attestation to require positive disclosure of outside business activities, private securities transactions, brokerage accounts, gifts received and any conflict, not just a read confirmation.
Run the completion report weekly and escalate outstanding names to the individual's supervisor at 30 days and to the Head of Compliance at 15 days before close.
Route every positive disclosure to the register owner - OBA and PST to Producer Compliance, accounts to personal trading surveillance, gifts to the gifts register.
checklist.done: every associated person has a dated attestation with positive disclosures routed to the correct register.

checklist.step: Maintain the conflicts of interest register
actions: Record each disclosed conflict with the person, the nature of the conflict, the business area affected, the mitigation applied and the approver.

Add the firm-level conflicts inherent to variable product distribution - proprietary product incentives, revenue sharing, sales contests and non-cash compensation under Rule 2320(g) and Rule 2341 - with the controls applied to each.
Review every open conflict at least annually and re-confirm or retire the mitigation with a dated note.
Report new material conflicts to the Compliance Committee in the quarter they are identified.
checklist.done: the register holds every disclosed and firm-level conflict with a dated mitigation, approver and annual re-confirmation.

checklist.step: Operate personal trading surveillance under Rule 3210
actions: Reconcile the declared brokerage account list from the attestation to the accounts for which the firm holds written prior consent under Rule 3210(a).
Chase the executing member for duplicate confirmations and account statements for every declared account and record receipt quarterly.
Review transactions for trading ahead of firm recommendations, restricted list breaches and undisclosed accounts, and escalate hits to the Ethics Officer within 5 business days.
File the quarterly surveillance report and the exception list in the binder section.
checklist.done: every declared account has written consent and current duplicate statements, and each quarter's surveillance report is filed.

checklist.step: Maintain the gifts and business entertainment register
actions: Record every gift given or received with the recipient, the counterparty firm, the value, the date and the business purpose.
Aggregate by recipient per twelve-month period and test against the Rule 3220 limit of 100 dollars per person per year, flagging every aggregate at or above the limit.
Separate business entertainment from gifts and confirm each entertainment event was attended by the firm host, as the rule expects.
Escalate every breach to the Ethics Officer with the proposed remedy - reimbursement, return of the gift or supervisory action.
checklist.done: the register aggregates by recipient per twelve months, tests against the 100 dollar Rule 3220 limit and escalates every breach.

checklist.step: Maintain outside business activity and private securities transaction records
actions: Log every Rule 3270 outside business activity notice with the activity, the entity, the compensation, the time commitment and the firm's written decision to approve, approve with conditions or prohibit.
Log every Rule 3280 private securities transaction notice, the firm's written approval or disapproval, and where approved, the supervision and record-keeping the firm applies to the transaction.
Cross-check the register against public sources for the sampled registered persons - state insurance producer appointments in NIPR and business registrations - to find undisclosed activity.
Confirm every approved activity is reflected on the individual's Form U4 where disclosure is required and file the amendment within 30 days.
checklist.done: every OBA and PST notice has a written firm decision, is cross-checked against external sources and is reflected on Form U4 where required.

checklist.step: Refresh the best execution review evidence under Rule 5310
actions: Obtain the regular and rigorous execution quality review for each quarter, covering the market centres used, price improvement, speed of execution, fill rates and likelihood of execution.
Confirm the review compares the routing arrangements actually used against competing market centres and states a conclusion with the reviewer name and date.

Confirm any payment for order flow or other routing inducement is disclosed in the review and considered in the conclusion, and that no interpositioning occurred without a documented benefit to the customer.
File the signed quarterly review in the binder section and record the date it was tabled at the Best Execution Committee.
checklist.done: each quarter holds a signed regular and rigorous review comparing market centres with a stated conclusion and committee tabling date.

checklist.step: Refresh the VA suitability and supervision evidence set
actions: Assemble the Rule 2330 evidence: principal review queue exports showing decision within 7 business days, the exchange comparison worksheets and the 36-month prior-exchange responses.
Add the suitability documentation set - customer investment profile, liquidity needs, the rider elections and the disclosure delivery record.
Add the surveillance reports on representatives with elevated exchange or surrender rates and the actions taken.
File the set in the binder section with a monthly refresh and a stated data-as-at date.
checklist.done: the VA section holds current principal review, exchange comparison, suitability and surveillance evidence with a monthly as-at date.

checklist.step: Refresh the complaint and correspondence evidence
actions: Export the Rule 4513 complaint register for the current and prior four quarters with complainant, date received, nature and disposition.
Attach the underlying complaint files for every complaint alleging sales practice or suitability, with the investigation notes and the response letter.
Confirm each complaint that met a Rule 4530 category was reported and cross-reference the report to the register row.
File the export and index in the binder section with a monthly refresh.
checklist.done: the complaint section holds a current Rule 4513 register, the sales-practice files and the Rule 4530 cross-reference.

checklist.step: Run a mock production drill on two binder sections each quarter
actions: Choose two binder sections at random each quarter and issue a mock examiner request to the named owner with no advance warning.
Time production from request to delivery and check the delivered pack is complete, indexed, dated and legible without further explanation.
Record failures - unfindable evidence, stale refresh, owner unaware of ownership - as exceptions with the elapsed time.
Report the drill results to the Head of Compliance with the elapsed times against the 5 business day standard.
checklist.done: two sections per quarter are drilled unannounced with elapsed production time recorded against the 5 business day standard.

checklist.step: Run the live exam production log when a request list arrives
actions: Open a production log on receipt of the FINRA request letter with one row per numbered request, the binder section, the owner, the internal due date backed off the letter deadline, and the status.
Route every draft production through General Counsel for privilege and scope review before delivery, and record the clearance date on the row.
Deliver only through the logged channel to the named examiner, capturing what was sent, when, and the file hashes or document counts.
Escalate any request that cannot be met by the letter deadline to the Head of Compliance and request an extension from the examiner in writing before the date passes.
checklist.done: every numbered request has a log row, a privilege clearance date, a delivery record and either an on-time delivery or a written extension.

checklist.step: Log readiness gaps as exceptions
actions: Raise an issue for every stale binder section, failed drill, missing attestation, undisclosed account or activity, and Rule 3220 breach.
Assign a root cause (owner change, evidence never produced by the process, register not fed, individual conduct) and a named owner.
Set a remediation date inside 60 days and, for undisclosed activity or accounts, require a Rule 4530 reportability assessment by Regulatory Counsel.
Report open items to the Compliance Committee with age and owner each quarter.
checklist.done: every readiness gap has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a 60-day remediation date and a reportability assessment where required.

checklist.step: Retain the binder and the exam correspondence record
actions: File each binder section version, the production logs and all examiner correspondence under Exam readiness / <year>.
Apply the 6-year FINRA Rule 4511 and SEA Rule 17a-4 retention label, keeping the first two years readily accessible.
Confirm the index shows last-refreshed date and owner per section and that superseded versions remain retrievable.
Confirm write-once storage or a tamper-evident audit trail is applied to produced documents so what was sent to the examiner cannot be altered.
checklist.done: the binder and exam correspondence are retained 6 years, indexed by section and owner, with produced documents tamper-evident.

testing.step: Build the population of binder sections and attestation-covered persons
actions: Export the binder index with section, owner, refresh frequency, last-refreshed date and evidence artifact.
Take the associated person roster from FINRA Gateway as at the test date as the attestation population.
Compare the index to the most recent FINRA cycle exam request list and list every requested category with no binder section.
Sign the population as complete before sampling.
testing.done: the section and person populations are extracted, compared to the live FINRA request list, and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile binder currency to the stated refresh frequencies
actions: For every section, compute days since last refresh and compare to the stated frequency.
List every section overdue and every section whose owner has left the firm per the HR leaver report.
Confirm the last-refreshed date on the index matches the actual document date inside the section, not just an index entry.
Record the currency percentage in the workpaper.
testing.done: currency is quantified per section and every overdue, orphaned or falsely dated section is listed.

testing.step: Draw the section and person sample
actions: Take 100 percent of the sections covering code of conduct, personal trading, gifts, outside activities and best execution.
Take 10 further sections and 25 associated persons by seeded random selection.
Record the seed, population size, selection date and selector so the sample can be redrawn.
Confirm no sampled section is owned by a member of the test team.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all conduct-critical sections, and is free of self-review.

testing.step: Re-perform an unannounced production request on the sampled sections
actions: Issue a written request to each sampled section owner for the named evidence artifact, with no advance notice and no help from the binder index.
Time delivery from request to receipt in business days and compare to the 5 business day internal standard.
Inspect each pack for completeness, dating, legibility and whether it answers the request without narration.
Record the elapsed time and the completeness result per section in the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled section has a timed, independently judged production result against the 5 business day standard.

testing.step: Reconcile attestation completion to the registered person roster
actions: Join the FINRA Gateway roster to the learning management system attestation register and compute the completion percentage.
List every associated person with no attestation for the period and check whether they joined after the campaign closed.
For 15 sampled attestations, confirm the record captures the positive disclosure answers, not just a read confirmation.
Confirm every positive disclosure was routed to and appears on the matching register.
testing.done: completion is measured off the FINRA roster and every positive disclosure is traced onto its register.

testing.step: Test personal trading and outside activity records against external sources
actions: For the 25 sampled persons, check the Rule 3210 declared account list against the duplicate statements actually received and against the written consents on file.
Check each person's insurance producer appointments in NIPR Gateway and any business registrations against the Rule 3270 outside activity register.
Compare each person's Form U4 disclosures in FINRA Gateway to the approved activities on the register.
Record every undisclosed account, activity or U4 mismatch as a reportable failure with the person named.
testing.done: each sampled person is checked against duplicate statements, NIPR appointments and Form U4, with mismatches reported.

testing.step: Recompute the Rule 3220 gift aggregation
actions: Rebuild the gift totals per recipient over a rolling twelve months from the raw gift log and any expense system entries coded to client gifts.
Compare your aggregate to the register aggregate and list every recipient at or over the 100 dollar limit that the register did not flag.
Check whether items recorded as business entertainment were actually attended by a firm host and reclassify those that were not.
Record the recomputed totals and the reclassifications in the workpaper.
testing.done: gift aggregation is independently recomputed over twelve months and unflagged limit breaches and misclassified entertainment are listed.

testing.step: Re-perform the best execution conclusion for one quarter
actions: Take one quarter's regular and rigorous review and confirm it names the market centres used, the comparison venues and the execution quality factors considered.
Recompute the routing share by venue from the order routing data and confirm it matches the review.
Confirm any routing inducement is disclosed and considered, and that any interpositioning is supported by a documented customer benefit.
Record whether the stated conclusion is supported by the underlying comparison or is unevidenced.
testing.done: the sampled best execution review is independently re-performed and its conclusion is either supported or challenged in writing.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the binder section or the individual, and what was missing or late.
Assign a root cause (owner change, register not fed, evidence never produced, individual non-disclosure) and an owner at manager level or above.
Set a remediation date inside 60 days and, for undisclosed accounts or activities, require a Rule 4530 reportability assessment and a Form U4 amendment decision from Regulatory Counsel.
Carry every open exception into the next semi-annual test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a 60-day remediation date and, where relevant, a reportability assessment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the exam readiness test
actions: Compare results to the thresholds: 100 percent of sections current and produced within 5 business days, 100 percent attestation completion, zero undisclosed accounts or activities.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper references behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who owns no binder section, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Compliance Committee and the General Counsel and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion, the currency and production percentages and the undisclosed-activity count.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the response to and remediation of FINRA examination findings - exam report exception letters, Cautionary Action Letters and Rule 8210 request outcomes - across the broker-dealer distributing variable products

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - the finding letter is read against the rule it cites, commonly FINRA Rule 1240(b) Firm Element, Rule 2210(d)(1) content standards and Rule 2211 variable product communications, with the rulebook text checked at the date of the conduct rather than the date of the letter

In-scope processes.value: Event-driven intake of every FINRA examination finding, self-regulatory inquiry and Rule 8210 request; root cause analysis, corrective action design, look-back over the affected population, customer remediation where harm occurred, and closure evidence back to the examiner

In-scope systems.value: Findings and remediation actions tracked in the GRC platform with the finding letter, response, action plan and closure evidence attached; look-back populations built from the policy administration platform and the marketing automation platform

Compliance procedure documented.value: Regulatory Findings Remediation Procedure - intake and logging on receipt, response drafting and legal clearance, root cause standard, action plan content standard, look-back scoping rule, customer remediation trigger, and evidence-based closure with independent validation

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and the General Counsel; reviewed after each completed examination cycle so the procedure absorbs what the last exam exposed

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Written response to a FINRA exam report exception letter or Cautionary Action Letter is due by the date stated in the letter, commonly within 30 calendar days of the letter date; Rule 8210 requests carry their own stated date; internal action plans are due within 10 business days of the response and remediation milestones are tracked to the dates committed in the response

Deadline reminders configured.value: Alerts at day 7, day 15 and day 25 of the 30 calendar day response clock, a milestone alert 10 business days before every committed remediation date, and a weekly overdue report to the Head of Compliance

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Finding letters, firm responses, action plans, look-back populations and results, customer remediation records and closure validations retained 6 years under FINRA Rule 4511 and SEA Rule 17a-4, indexed by exam number

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Every finding is a tracked item; missed committed dates, actions closed without evidence and repeat findings from a prior cycle are separately flagged with root cause and escalation

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Clears every written response to FINRA before it is sent and signs off closure of any finding involving customer harm, a Rule 4530 reportable event or a repeat of a prior-cycle finding

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every FINRA examination finding, Cautionary Action Letter item and Rule 8210 request received in the period, together with every remediation action and look-back population arising from them

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero responses sent after the letter deadline without a written extension; zero actions closed without objective evidence; any repeat of a prior-cycle finding is an automatic fail regardless of the current action status

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is event-driven; the test runs quarterly over all findings open or closed in the quarter, and in full after each examination cycle closes

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Validation must be performed by someone who neither drafted the response nor owned any remediation action being closed

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly findings remediation test workpaper (findings population, response timeliness recomputation, closure evidence re-performance, repeat-finding analysis, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Per-finding pack holding the letter, the cleared response, the action plan with owners and dates, the look-back population and results, customer remediation evidence and the independent closure validation, producible to FINRA within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Head of Compliance signs the response to FINRA after General Counsel clearance; all correspondence goes through the single logged channel to the named examiner, and any request for an extension is made in writing before the stated deadline passes

checklist.step: Log the finding the day the letter arrives
actions: Open a finding record on the day of receipt with the letter date, exam number, examiner name, the rule cited, the finding text quoted verbatim and the stated response deadline.
Compute the response due date as letter date plus the days stated in the letter, commonly 30 calendar days, and set alerts at day 7, 15 and 25.
Assign a business owner at manager level or above for each numbered finding and notify them and the Head of Compliance the same day.
Attach the letter and any accompanying exhibits to the record.
checklist.done: every numbered finding has a record created on the receipt date with a computed due date, alerts and a named business owner.

checklist.step: Verify the factual basis of each finding before responding
actions: Pull the underlying records the examiner relied on - the sampled files, communications, principal review records or training records - and confirm each stated fact.
Read the cited rule text as it stood on the date of the conduct, not the date of the letter, and note any intervening rule change.
Where a stated fact is wrong, assemble the contradicting evidence with document identifiers rather than argument.
Record for each finding: accepted, accepted in part with the correction, or disputed with evidence.
checklist.done: each finding carries an accepted, part-accepted or disputed position supported by named source documents.

checklist.step: Run the root cause analysis to a stated standard
actions: Run a structured five-whys or fault-tree session with the business owner, the supervising principal and the process performer, and minute it.
Classify the root cause as procedure gap, supervision failure, system control gap, training gap, capacity, or individual conduct - never as human error alone.
Test whether the same cause could produce failures in adjacent processes and list those processes for the look-back scope.
Record the root cause and the adjacent-process list on the finding record before the action plan is written.
checklist.done: each finding has a classified root cause from a minuted session and a list of adjacent processes at risk from the same cause.

checklist.step: Scope and build the look-back population
actions: Set the look-back window from the date the control weakness began - the procedure version date, system release date or supervisor change date - to the date the interim control was applied.
Extract the full affected population from the policy administration platform and, for communications findings, from the marketing automation platform, keyed by customer, representative and date.
Reconcile the extract to the source system totals for the window and record the row count and reconciliation on the finding record.
Hand the population to the business owner with the fields needed to judge whether each item was actually deficient.
checklist.done: the look-back window is justified by a dated control event and the reconciled affected population is produced.

checklist.step: Draft the written response to FINRA
actions: Draft a response addressing every numbered finding in the order the letter uses, stating the firm position, the corrective action, the owner and the completion date.
State the look-back scope and its status, and commit to reporting the outcome by a named date rather than leaving it open.
Where customer harm is possible, state the remediation approach and the population size rather than deferring the question.
Circulate to the business owners for factual confirmation, then to the General Counsel for clearance.
checklist.done: a draft response answers every numbered finding with a corrective action, an owner and a committed completion date.

checklist.step: Clear and send the response before the deadline
actions: Confirm General Counsel clearance is recorded before the response is sent, and that no commitment in the response exceeds what the firm can actually deliver.
Send through the logged channel to the named examiner on or before the date stated in the letter, and capture the delivery confirmation.
Where the deadline cannot be met, request an extension in writing from the examiner before the date passes and record the written grant.
Attach the sent response and the delivery confirmation to the finding record.
checklist.done: the response is sent on or before the stated deadline, or a written extension pre-dates it, with delivery evidence attached.

checklist.step: Convert every commitment into a tracked action
actions: Within 10 business days of sending the response, create one action per commitment with the exact wording used to the regulator, the owner, the due date and the closure evidence expected.
Split multi-part commitments so a partly delivered action cannot show as complete.
Link every action to its finding record and to the root cause so themes across findings are visible.
Set milestone alerts 10 business days before each committed date.
checklist.done: every commitment made to FINRA exists as a discrete tracked action with owner, date and named closure evidence.

checklist.step: Put an interim control in place while the permanent fix is built
actions: For each finding, agree an interim control with the business owner that stops recurrence now - 100 percent principal pre-approval, a manual second review, a hold on the product or communication type.
Document the interim control, its start date, who operates it and how its operation is evidenced.
Confirm the interim control is running by sampling its output in the first week and again in the fourth week.
Keep the interim control live until the permanent action is closed and independently validated, not until it is merely delivered.
checklist.done: each finding has a dated, evidenced interim control that stays live until the permanent action is validated.

checklist.step: Deliver the permanent corrective action
actions: Deliver the fix the root cause requires - WSP amendment with a named principal, a system control or validation, a supervisory report, a targeted training module, or added supervisory capacity.
For WSP amendments, route through the standard approval and attestation route so the change reaches the supervisors who must operate it.
For system controls, obtain the change record and the test evidence from the delivering team.
Attach the delivery evidence to the action and set it to Delivered, not Closed.
checklist.done: each corrective action is delivered with objective evidence attached and is marked Delivered pending validation.

checklist.step: Complete the look-back and quantify the affected customers
actions: Review the look-back population against the standard the rule requires and classify each item compliant, deficient or deficient with potential customer detriment.
For communications findings, re-review each retail piece against Rule 2210(d)(1) content standards and Rule 2211 variable product requirements and list the items that would fail today.
For training findings, identify every registered person who should have received the Firm Element content and did not.
Report the counts, the detriment population and the proposed remediation to the Head of Compliance and Regulatory Counsel.
checklist.done: the look-back is completed with items classified and the customer-detriment population quantified and reported.

checklist.step: Remediate customers where detriment is found
actions: Design the remedy with Regulatory Counsel - corrective disclosure, surrender charge reimbursement, contract rescission or rider restoration - with a stated calculation basis.
Build the customer list with the amount per customer, the calculation and the approval of the Head of Compliance and the Chief Financial Officer for the total.
Issue the corrective communication and the payment, tracking delivery, returned mail and unclaimed amounts to conclusion.
Record each customer, amount, date and delivery evidence in the case management tool as the remediation register.
checklist.done: every detrimented customer has a calculated remedy, an issued communication or payment and a delivery record.

checklist.step: Assess reportability and any parallel obligation
actions: Assess each finding against the FINRA Rule 4530(b) categories and file within 30 calendar days of the firm concluding a violation has occurred.
Assess whether any individual conduct requires a Form U4 or Form U5 disclosure amendment and file within the 30 day requirement.
Assess whether the same conduct triggers a state insurance department notification for the variable products involved.
Record each assessment with the conclusion and the filing reference, including a reasoned no-filing conclusion.
checklist.done: each finding carries a reasoned reportability assessment with any Rule 4530, U4 or U5 filing reference recorded.

checklist.step: Validate closure independently before marking the finding closed
actions: For each Delivered action, test the control in operation over a sample of at least one full cycle after delivery, not just the delivery artifact.
Confirm the tested outcome addresses the root cause recorded on the finding, not just the symptom the examiner saw.
Confirm the look-back and any customer remediation is complete, with unresolved items separately tracked.
Sign a validation note per action; only a signed validation moves an action from Delivered to Closed.
checklist.done: no action reaches Closed without a signed validation note evidencing the control operating after delivery.

checklist.step: Report status and escalate slippage
actions: Report to the Compliance Committee monthly: findings open, actions overdue against dates committed to FINRA, look-back status and customer remediation progress.
Escalate any action that will miss a date committed to the regulator to the Committee before the date passes and decide whether to notify the examiner.
Track repeat findings from prior cycles separately and present them as a governance issue, not a process issue.
Record decisions, owners and dates in the minutes and post the pack to the board portal.
checklist.done: monthly reporting shows overdue actions against regulator-committed dates and every likely miss is escalated before it happens.

checklist.step: Close the exam file and retain the record
actions: Assemble the per-finding pack - letter, response, action plan, delivery evidence, look-back results, remediation register, validation notes and the closing correspondence from FINRA.
File under Exams / <exam number> / <finding number> in the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 6-year FINRA Rule 4511 retention label and confirm searchability by exam number, rule cited and root cause.
Feed the root cause themes into the next annual WSP review and the next Firm Element needs analysis.
checklist.done: each finding pack is complete, filed under the exam number, retention-labelled and its root cause fed into the annual review cycle.

testing.step: Build the complete population of regulatory findings
actions: Extract every finding record open or closed in the period from the GRC platform with letter date, exam number, rule cited, owner and status.
Independently sweep the regulatory correspondence mailbox, the General Counsel matter list and the examiner correspondence log for letters that never became a record.
Reconcile the two lists and treat every letter with no record as a completeness failure.
Sign the population as complete before sampling.
testing.done: the findings population is reconciled to source correspondence and every unlogged letter is recorded as a completeness failure.

testing.step: Recompute response timeliness against each letter deadline
actions: For every finding, read the deadline stated in the letter and recompute the due date from the letter date.
Compare the actual send date on the delivery confirmation and compute days early or late.
For any late response, confirm a written extension exists and that it was granted before the original deadline passed.
List every response sent late without a pre-dated written extension as a fail.
testing.done: response timeliness is recomputed for every finding and unextended late responses are failed.

testing.step: Draw the finding and action sample
actions: Take 100 percent of findings involving customer harm, Rule 4530 reportability or a repeat of a prior-cycle finding.
Take 15 further actions closed in the period by seeded random selection.
Record the seed, population size, selection date and selector so the sample can be redrawn.
Confirm no sampled action was owned or validated by a member of the test team.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all harm and repeat findings, and is free of self-review.

testing.step: Re-perform the closure test on sampled actions
actions: For each sampled closed action, ignore the validation note and test the control yourself over a sample of transactions dated after the delivery date.
Confirm the control operates as the response to FINRA described it, using the same wording as the commitment.
Treat an action closed on a delivery artifact alone, with no post-delivery operating evidence, as a fail.
Record the tested period, the sample and the result per action.
testing.done: each sampled closure is independently re-performed on post-delivery transactions and evidence-free closures are failed.

testing.step: Trace the look-back scope and completeness
actions: For each sampled finding, confirm the look-back start date is justified by a dated control event rather than chosen for convenience.
Rebuild the affected population from the policy administration platform for the same window and compare your row count to the firm's.
Check the classification of 20 look-back items against the rule standard and note any deficient item classified compliant.
List any look-back that stopped short of the adjacent processes named in the root cause analysis.
testing.done: each sampled look-back has a justified window, a reconciled population and independently checked item classifications.

testing.step: Test the customer remediation register
actions: Reconcile the remediation register to the detriment population from the look-back and list every customer in one but not the other.
Recompute the remedy amount for 15 customers using the stated calculation basis and compare to the amount paid.
Trace payment or corrective communication evidence per sampled customer, including returned mail handling and unclaimed balances.
Confirm the total paid reconciles to the general ledger entry and to the approval obtained.
testing.done: the register reconciles to the detriment population, recomputed amounts agree and every sampled payment is traced to evidence.

testing.step: Test reportability decisions
actions: For each sampled finding, read the Rule 4530 assessment and form your own view against the Rule 4530(b) categories.
Where a filing was made, recompute the 30 calendar day clock from the date the firm concluded a violation occurred to the FINRA Gateway filing date.
Where no filing was made, confirm the reasoning is written and reasoned rather than absent.
Check any related Form U4 or U5 amendment was filed within its 30 day requirement.
testing.done: every sampled reportability decision is independently re-formed and every filing clock is recomputed.

testing.step: Analyse repeat findings across cycles
actions: Compare the current period findings to the prior two examination cycles on rule cited and root cause.
List every finding that repeats a prior finding and check whether the earlier action was validated closed and whether the validation was sound.
For each repeat, judge whether the earlier root cause was misclassified or the fix was never operated.
Report every repeat to the Compliance Committee as a governance failure regardless of the current action status.
testing.done: repeat findings are identified across three cycles with a written judgement on why the earlier fix did not hold.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the exam number, the finding number and what failed - late response, unevidenced closure, truncated look-back, missed remediation, missed filing.
Assign a root cause and an owner at manager level or above, and for repeat findings escalate ownership to the executive accountable for the process.
Set a remediation date and require post-delivery operating evidence, not a delivery artifact, for closure.
Carry every open exception into the next quarterly test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an escalated owner where repeated, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the remediation test
actions: Compare results to the thresholds: zero unextended late responses, zero closures without post-delivery evidence, zero repeat findings.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper references behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who neither drafted a response nor owned a sampled action, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Compliance Committee and the General Counsel and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under the exam number.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion, the late-response and unevidenced-closure counts and the repeat-finding list.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the written business continuity plan required by FINRA Rule 4370 and the emergency contact information the firm maintains with FINRA, for the broker-dealer entity

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - FINRA Rule 4370(c) plan elements, Rule 4370(e) customer disclosure, Rule 4370(f) annual review, Rule 4370(g) emergency contact information and Rule 4517 contact information maintenance, re-read at the start of each annual review

In-scope processes.value: Annual review and approval of the broker-dealer BCP, maintenance of the two FINRA emergency contacts in the FINRA Contact System, customer BCP disclosure at account opening and on the firm website, and the change-driven refresh of mission critical system and critical business constituent lists

In-scope systems.value: BCP master and approval record in the compliance evidence repository; emergency contacts maintained in FINRA Gateway (FINRA Contact System); mission critical system and dependency data drawn from the CMDB; customer disclosure published on the firm website and the customer self-service portal

Compliance procedure documented.value: Business Continuity Plan Maintenance Procedure - element-by-element ownership against Rule 4370(c), the annual review and senior-management approval route, the FINRA Contact System update rule, the customer disclosure route and the trigger list for out-of-cycle updates

Compliance procedure approved.value: The plan itself is approved annually by a member of senior management as Rule 4370(b) requires; the maintenance procedure is approved by the Head of Compliance and the Chief Operating Officer

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual BCP review and senior management approval each calendar year under Rule 4370(f); FINRA Contact System contacts reviewed and verified within 17 business days after the end of each calendar year under Rule 4517(b); any change to the designated emergency contacts updated promptly and within 30 days, with an internal standard of 10 business days

Deadline reminders configured.value: Annual review kick-off alert on 1 September against a 31 December approval date, an FCS verification alert on 2 January running to the 17 business day deadline, and an immediate alert on any HR leaver record naming a designated emergency contact

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Every BCP version, the annual review record, the senior management approval, FCS update confirmations and the customer disclosure versions retained 6 years under FINRA Rule 4511 and SEA Rule 17a-4

checklist.step: Open the annual review and rebuild the element cross-reference
actions: Open the current plan and build a matrix with one row per Rule 4370(c) element: data back-up and recovery (hard copy and electronic), mission critical systems, financial and operational assessments, alternate communications between the firm and customers, alternate communications between the firm and employees, alternate physical location of employees, critical business constituent, bank and counter-party impact, regulatory reporting, and communications with regulators.
For each row record the plan section, the named owner, the last update date and the evidence that the arrangement actually exists.
Mark every row where the plan asserts a capability with no supporting arrangement as NOT EVIDENCED and hand the list to the Operational Risk Manager.
Set the review timetable against a 31 December approval date with kick-off on 1 September.
checklist.done: the matrix covers every Rule 4370(c) element with a plan section, owner, update date and an evidence reference or a NOT EVIDENCED flag.

checklist.step: Refresh the mission critical systems list from the CMDB
actions: Export the application inventory from the CMDB with business service, criticality tier, hosting model, recovery time objective and recovery point objective.
Confirm every system that supports order taking, order entry, execution, clearance, customer access to funds and securities, and books and records is tiered mission critical.
Reconcile the CMDB tiering to the business impact analysis owners and resolve every disagreement in writing before the list is frozen.
Publish the agreed mission critical list into the plan appendix with the RTO and RPO on each row.
checklist.done: the mission critical list is CMDB-sourced, agreed with business owners and carries an RTO and RPO per system.

checklist.step: Refresh the critical business constituent, bank and counterparty list
actions: List the clearing firm, the annuity issuers, the transfer agent, the banks holding firm and customer funds, the market data and order routing vendors and the books and records service providers.
For each, record the service, the contractual recovery commitment, the date their own BCP or resilience attestation was last obtained, and the alternate arrangement if they fail.
Chase any constituent whose attestation is older than twelve months and record the chase and the response.
Write the refreshed list and the alternate arrangements into the plan appendix.
checklist.done: every critical constituent has a recorded recovery commitment, a current resilience attestation and a named alternate arrangement.

checklist.step: Update the data back-up and recovery arrangements
actions: Confirm the plan states where hard copy and electronic books and records are backed up, at what frequency and to which geographically separate location.

Confirm the electronic records retained under SEA Rule 17a-4 are held in the required non-rewriteable format or with an audit-trail alternative, and name the third party holding the undertaking letter where one is required.
Record the last successful restore test date for each mission critical data set and flag anything untested in the last twelve months.
Update the plan section with the confirmed arrangements and the restore evidence references.
checklist.done: back-up locations, frequency, record format compliance and last restore test dates are stated in the plan and evidenced.

checklist.step: Refresh the alternate communications and location arrangements
actions: Confirm the customer communication routes in a disruption - the customer self-service portal notice, the recorded phone message script, the website banner and the contact centre overflow arrangement - and name who activates each.
Confirm the employee communication route including the mass notification tool, the call tree and the out-of-band channel if corporate email is unavailable.
Confirm the alternate physical location for each critical team with its capacity, distance from the primary site and activation lead time.
Record the arrangements with owners and activation triggers in the plan.
checklist.done: customer routes, employee routes and alternate sites each name an owner, a trigger and an activation lead time.

checklist.step: Confirm customer access to funds and securities is addressed
actions: State in the plan how customers reach their funds and securities if the firm cannot operate, including the clearing firm route and the direct-to-issuer route for variable contracts.
Confirm with the clearing firm and the annuity issuers, in writing, that the stated route works and record the confirmation date.
State the procedure for prompt customer notification of the alternate route, including the wording and the channel.
Where the firm determines a disruption route is not practicable, state that determination and the reason in the plan as Rule 4370(d) contemplates.
checklist.done: the plan states a written, counterparty-confirmed route to customer funds and securities, or a documented determination that it is not practicable.

checklist.step: Update the regulatory reporting continuity section
actions: List the regulatory reports the firm must continue to make in a disruption - FOCUS reports, Rule 4530 filings, blue sheet requests, MCAS - with their deadlines and their filing channels.
Name the alternate preparer and the alternate submission route for each, including manual filing where the primary system is unavailable.
State the escalation route for requesting relief or an extension from FINRA or the SEC and name who makes that contact.
Write the section into the plan with the owner and the contact detail per report.
checklist.done: each continuing regulatory report has an alternate preparer, an alternate channel and a named relief-request owner.

checklist.step: Verify and update the FINRA emergency contacts
actions: Log in to FINRA Gateway and open the FINRA Contact System to view the firm's designated emergency contacts.
Confirm two emergency contacts are designated, that both are members of senior management and executive representatives, and that at least one is a registered principal.
Update name, title, mobile number, email and an out-of-band contact where any detail has changed, using the internal 10 business day standard and never later than the 30 day requirement.
Verify the full contact record within 17 business days after the end of the calendar year as Rule 4517(b) requires and save the confirmation screen as evidence.
checklist.done: two qualifying emergency contacts are current in the FINRA Contact System with an annual verification saved inside 17 business days of year end.

checklist.step: Publish the customer BCP disclosure
actions: Refresh the plain-language BCP disclosure summarising how the firm will respond to disruptions of varying scope and how customers can reach their funds and securities.
Publish it on the firm website and the customer self-service portal and record the publication date and the page URL.
Confirm the account opening pack delivers the disclosure to every new customer and that the delivery is recorded on the account record.
Confirm the mail-on-request route is staffed and its service level stated, and add the disclosure to the annual customer communications calendar.
checklist.done: the disclosure is published, delivered at account opening with a recorded delivery, and available on request through a staffed route.

checklist.step: Reconcile the plan to the current organisation
actions: Take the HR leaver, joiner and transfer report for the year and check every named individual in the plan, the call tree and the recovery teams is still in role.
Check every branch and OSJ on the Form BR list appears in the site recovery arrangements.
Check every system added or retired in the year is reflected in the mission critical list.
Correct the plan and record each correction with its trigger so out-of-cycle changes are traceable.
checklist.done: the plan names only current individuals, sites and systems, with each correction traced to its trigger.

checklist.step: Route the plan to senior management for annual approval
actions: Review the element matrix, the NOT EVIDENCED list, the test results from the resilience testing programme and the open gaps before signing.
Sign the approval page naming the plan version, the approval date and the elements reviewed, so the Rule 4370(b) senior management approval is explicit.
Direct remediation on any element left unevidenced, with an owner and a date, rather than approving around it.
Confirm the approval date falls inside the calendar year so the Rule 4370(f) annual review is met.
checklist.done: a dated senior management approval names the version and the elements and is signed inside the calendar year.

checklist.step: Publish the approved plan and brief the recovery teams
actions: Publish the approved version to the compliance evidence repository, lock the prior version read-only and both remain retrievable.
Distribute the version to recovery team leads, branch managers and the emergency contacts, and record acknowledgement.
Store an offline copy - printed or on offline media at the alternate site - so the plan survives loss of the primary environment.
Update the WSP business continuity section to cite the new plan version number.
checklist.done: the approved version is published, acknowledged, available offline and cited by version number in the WSP.

checklist.step: Operate the out-of-cycle update triggers
actions: Subscribe the plan to the change triggers: material change to business, structure, operations or location, clearing firm change, new mission critical system, emergency contact departure.
On each trigger, update the affected section within 30 days and record the trigger, the change and the update date.
Where the change affects the FINRA emergency contacts, make the FINRA Contact System update inside the 10 business day internal standard.
Report all out-of-cycle updates to the Chief Operating Officer at the next quarterly resilience review.
checklist.done: each triggering change produces a dated plan update within 30 days and an FCS update where contacts changed.

checklist.step: Log plan and contact gaps as exceptions
actions: Raise an issue for every NOT EVIDENCED element, missing constituent attestation, untested restore, stale emergency contact and undelivered customer disclosure.
Assign a root cause (arrangement never built, owner change, vendor non-response, process not wired to account opening) and an owner at manager level or above.
Set a remediation date inside 90 days and require the underlying arrangement, not a plan wording change, as closure evidence.
Report the open list to the Chief Operating Officer and the Compliance Committee each quarter.
checklist.done: every gap has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a 90-day date and an arrangement-based closure requirement.

checklist.step: Retain the plan and approval record
actions: File the approved version, the element matrix, the constituent attestations, the FCS confirmation and the approval page under BCP / <year>.
Apply the 6-year FINRA Rule 4511 and SEA Rule 17a-4 retention label with the first two years readily accessible.
Confirm superseded versions remain retrievable and that the index shows version, approval date and approver.
Confirm the offline copy location is recorded in the index.
checklist.done: the plan record is retained 6 years, versioned with approver and date, and the offline copy location is indexed.

testing.step: Build the population of plan elements, systems and constituents
actions: Take the approved plan version under test and list every Rule 4370(c) element, every mission critical system and every critical business constituent it names.
Independently pull the mission critical application list from the CMDB and the vendor list from the GRC platform and compare to the plan.
List every system or constituent the firm treats as critical elsewhere but the plan omits.
Sign the population as complete before sampling.
testing.done: an independently sourced system and constituent population is compared to the plan and omissions are itemised.

testing.step: Reconcile plan coverage to the Rule 4370(c) element list
actions: Read Rule 4370(c) directly from the FINRA rulebook and build your own element checklist rather than reusing the firm matrix.
Map each element to plan text and mark addressed, partially addressed or absent, quoting the plan sentence relied on.
Record any element the plan asserts but which the firm has determined is not practicable, and check the determination is stated as Rule 4370(d) requires.
Report the count of absent and partially addressed elements.
testing.done: every Rule 4370(c) element is independently mapped to quoted plan text with absent elements counted.

testing.step: Draw the sample of systems, constituents and accounts
actions: Take 100 percent of mission critical systems supporting customer access to funds and securities and books and records.
Take 10 critical business constituents and 25 new customer accounts opened in the year by seeded random selection.
Record the seed, population size, selection date and selector so the sample can be redrawn.
Confirm no sampled item was maintained by a member of the test team.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers the customer-access-critical systems and is free of self-review.

testing.step: Re-perform the evidence check behind the plan assertions
actions: For each sampled system, request the last restore or failover evidence and compare the achieved recovery time to the RTO stated in the plan.
For each sampled constituent, request the resilience attestation and the contractual recovery commitment and check the date and the content.
Where the plan asserts an arrangement and no evidence exists, record it as an unevidenced assertion, not a documentation gap.
Capture the evidence identifiers into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled assertion is either evidenced with a dated artifact or recorded as an unevidenced assertion.

testing.step: Verify the annual approval and the review date
actions: Open the approval page and confirm it names the plan version, the approval date and a member of senior management as Rule 4370(b) requires.
Confirm the approval date falls inside the calendar year and that the version approved is the version published.
Compare the published version hash or document identifier to the version in the repository index to prove no post-approval edit.
Record any approval that post-dates the year end or covers a superseded version as a fail.
testing.done: the approval is proven to name a senior manager, sit inside the calendar year and cover the published version.

testing.step: Re-perform the FINRA Contact System verification
actions: Open FINRA Gateway and view the FINRA Contact System emergency contact record for the firm.
Confirm two contacts are designated, both are senior management and executive representatives, and at least one is a registered principal with an active registration.
Compare the contact details against the current HR record and the phone directory and note any stale number or email.
Recompute the annual verification date against 17 business days after year end and record the days late if applicable.
testing.done: the FCS record is independently inspected, contact eligibility confirmed and the 17 business day verification recomputed.

testing.step: Test customer disclosure delivery on the account sample
actions: For each sampled new account, find the record of BCP disclosure delivery at account opening with the date and the method.
Open the firm website and the customer self-service portal and confirm the current disclosure is published and matches the approved version.
Place a test request through the mail-on-request route and record the response time against the stated service level.
List every sampled account with no disclosure delivery record as a fail.
testing.done: disclosure delivery is traced per sampled account, the published version is confirmed and the request route is response-tested.

testing.step: Test the out-of-cycle update discipline
actions: Take the year's material changes - clearing firm or vendor changes, new systems, site moves, senior leaver records - from the change and HR records.
Trace each to a dated plan update and compute the days from the change to the update against the 30 day expectation.
For any change affecting the emergency contacts, compute the days to the FCS update against the internal 10 business day standard and the 30 day requirement.
List every change with no corresponding plan update.
testing.done: each material change is traced to a dated plan update with the elapsed days computed, and unreflected changes are listed.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the element, system, constituent, contact or account and what was missing.
Assign a root cause (arrangement never built, vendor non-response, change not notified, account opening process gap) and an owner at manager level or above.
Set a remediation date inside 90 days and require the underlying arrangement or the corrected FCS record as closure evidence.
Carry every open exception into next year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a 90-day remediation date and an arrangement-based closure test.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the BCP compliance test
actions: Compare results to the thresholds: all Rule 4370(c) elements addressed, approval dated inside the calendar year by senior management, FCS verified within 17 business days of year end, zero accounts without disclosure.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper references behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who neither authored nor approved the plan version, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Compliance Committee and the Chief Operating Officer and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion, the element coverage result, the approval date and the FCS verification timing.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the annual resilience and disaster recovery test programme for the broker-dealer mission critical systems and the test results that feed the FINRA Rule 3120 supervisory controls report to senior management

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - FINRA Rule 3120(a) testing and verification of supervisory procedures and Rule 3120(b) the annual report to senior management, read alongside Rule 4370(f) annual BCP review, at the start of each test year

In-scope processes.value: Annual disaster recovery and resilience testing of mission critical systems - order entry and execution, customer access to funds and securities, variable annuity application and suitability review, books and records retention, and the market data and clearing interfaces - plus the reporting of test results into the annual Rule 3120 supervisory controls report

In-scope systems.value: Test plans, change records and defects raised in the ITSM platform; system availability and recovery telemetry from Grafana and Splunk SIEM; dependency and criticality data from the CMDB; results filed in the compliance evidence repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: Resilience Test Procedure - annual test calendar by system tier, scenario catalogue, entry and exit criteria, RTO and RPO measurement method, defect severity scale, retest rule and the reporting route into the Rule 3120 report

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Information Officer and the Chief Operating Officer, with the reporting route into the Rule 3120 report agreed with the Head of Compliance each year

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Every mission critical system tested at least once each calendar year; the Rule 3120 supervisory controls report, including the summary of test results, delivered to senior management at least annually; severity one defects retested within 30 days of the fix

Deadline reminders configured.value: Test calendar alerts 30 days before each scheduled window, an untested-system alert at 1 October for anything still untested in the year, and a Rule 3120 report drafting alert 60 days before the committed delivery date

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Test plans, run logs, telemetry captures, measured RTO and RPO, defect records, retest evidence and the Rule 3120 report retained 6 years under FINRA Rule 4511 and SEA Rule 17a-4

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Failed tests, systems untested in the calendar year, RTO or RPO misses and unretested severity one defects are logged as defects with owner, severity, remediation date and retest evidence

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off closure of every failed test and every RTO or RPO miss, and confirms the test result summary that goes into the Rule 3120 report

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every mission critical system on the CMDB tier one list for the calendar year, every scheduled test in the annual calendar, and every defect raised from a resilience test

Pass/fail thresholds.value: 100 percent of mission critical systems tested in the calendar year; measured recovery time must meet the stated RTO and data loss must meet the stated RPO - any miss is a failed test; any severity one defect not retested within 30 days of the fix is a fail; the Rule 3120 report must reach senior management within the calendar year

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual per system; the independent test runs annually after the test calendar closes, with a mid-year coverage check in July on systems still untested

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual resilience testing assurance workpaper (coverage matrix, observed test evidence, RTO and RPO recomputation, defect ageing, Rule 3120 report tracing) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Annual test calendar with per-system results, the measured RTO and RPO against target, the defect and retest log and the Rule 3120 report with its delivery record, producible to a FINRA examiner within 5 business days
