checklist.step: Build the annual test calendar from the mission critical inventory
actions: Export the tier one application list from the CMDB with business service, RTO, RPO, hosting model and upstream and downstream dependencies.
Schedule at least one test per system per calendar year, grouping systems that share a recovery domain so dependencies are exercised together.
Agree each window with the business service owner and the Contact Center Ops Manager so customer-facing outages are avoided or announced.
Publish the calendar with system, scenario, date, participants and the exit criteria for each test.
checklist.done: every tier one system has at least one scheduled test in the calendar year with an agreed window and stated exit criteria.

checklist.step: Choose scenarios that match real failure modes
actions: Take the scenario catalogue and select per system from: data centre or region loss, database corruption requiring point-in-time restore, ransomware requiring clean-room recovery, loss of a critical vendor connection, and loss of the primary work location.
Include at least one scenario per year that tests customer access to funds and securities end to end with the clearing firm and an annuity issuer.
Include at least one severe but plausible scenario that exceeds the standard recovery playbook so the escalation path is exercised.
Have the Operational Risk Manager confirm the selected scenarios cover the top operational risks on the risk register.
checklist.done: each system has a named scenario, the year includes an end-to-end customer access test and a severe but plausible scenario.

checklist.step: Write the test plan and fix the measurement method
actions: Write the plan with entry criteria, the failure injection method, the recovery steps to be followed from the runbook, the participants and the exit criteria.
Define exactly how recovery time is measured - from the declared failure timestamp to the point the business owner confirms the service is usable, not to the point the infrastructure is up.
Define how data loss is measured - the last committed transaction before failure against the last transaction present after recovery, evidenced from the transaction log.
Raise the test as a change record in the ITSM platform with the plan attached and the approvals recorded.
checklist.done: the plan states entry and exit criteria and defines RTO and RPO measurement to a business-usable point with evidence sources.

checklist.step: Confirm readiness before the window opens
actions: Verify the recovery environment capacity, the current backup restore points and the replication lag against the RPO on the day before the test.
Confirm the observability dashboards and the log capture in Splunk SIEM and Grafana will record the timeline at the granularity the measurement needs.
Confirm the runbook version to be used is the current one and that the participants can access it without the primary environment.
Sign the readiness checklist or defer the test rather than running it on a known-broken precondition.
checklist.done: readiness is signed with capacity, restore points, replication lag and observability confirmed, or the test is deferred.

checklist.step: Execute the test and timestamp every step
actions: Open a bridge with the participants, declare the scenario and record the failure injection timestamp.
Follow the runbook exactly as written and log every deviation, because a deviation is a runbook defect even when the recovery succeeds.
Record the timestamps for detection, declaration, recovery start, service restored and business confirmation.
Capture the supporting telemetry, console output and screenshots into the test record as the run happens rather than reconstructing later.
checklist.done: the run log holds timestamped detection, declaration, restoration and business confirmation with telemetry captured live.

checklist.step: Validate the recovered service with the business
actions: Run the agreed business validation script in the recovered environment - place a test order, complete a variable annuity application through principal review, produce a customer statement, retrieve a retained record.
Confirm integrations work in the recovered state: clearing firm connection, annuity issuer feed, market data, payment route.
Record pass or fail per validation step with the evidence, and only then declare service restored for the RTO measurement.
Report any function that recovered but with degraded capacity, stating the degradation.
checklist.done: business validation is executed step by step in the recovered environment with a recorded pass or fail and any degradation stated.

checklist.step: Measure RTO and RPO against target
actions: Compute achieved recovery time from the failure injection timestamp to the business confirmation timestamp and compare to the CMDB RTO.
Compute achieved data loss by comparing the last transaction identifier before failure with the last present after recovery, from the transaction log.
Record both against target with a pass or fail and, on failure, the specific step that consumed the time or lost the data.
Publish the measured values into the test record and the resilience dashboard.
checklist.done: achieved RTO and RPO are computed from timestamps and transaction identifiers and compared to the CMDB targets.

checklist.step: Raise defects with severity and owners
actions: Raise one defect per issue found - RTO or RPO miss, runbook deviation, missing access, absent dependency, unavailable participant - with the evidence attached.
Assign severity: one where the firm could not meet a recovery obligation, two where recovery succeeded but outside target, three for runbook or documentation defects.
Assign an owner and a due date - 30 days for severity one, 90 days for severity two - and a mandatory retest for severity one.
Notify the Chief Information Officer of every severity one defect on the day it is raised.
checklist.done: every finding is a severity-rated defect with an owner, a due date and a retest requirement on severity one.

checklist.step: Fix and retest the severity one defects
actions: Deliver the fix through the normal change route with the change record linked to the defect.
Retest the specific failure path within 30 days of the fix, using the same measurement method as the original test.
Where the retest cannot reproduce the original conditions, state that limitation on the record rather than declaring success.
Close the defect only on retest evidence signed by the Disaster Recovery Manager.
checklist.done: every severity one defect has a linked change, a retest inside 30 days using the same method, and a signed closure.

checklist.step: Include the critical vendors in the test programme
actions: Identify the vendors whose failure would stop a mission critical service - clearing firm, annuity issuers, market data, transfer agent, cloud hosting, books and records provider.
Obtain each vendor's own annual DR test summary or resilience attestation and record the date, the scenario tested and the result.
Arrange a joint connectivity or failover test with at least the clearing firm and one annuity issuer each year and record the outcome.
Escalate any vendor refusing to evidence testing to the Vendor Manager and the Operational Risk Manager for contractual action.
checklist.done: every mission critical vendor has a dated test summary on file and a joint test is completed with the clearing firm and an issuer.

checklist.step: Review results at the resilience governance forum
actions: Present each quarter: tests completed against calendar, achieved RTO and RPO against target, open defects by severity and age, and vendor test status.
Escalate any system untested by 1 October and force a window before year end rather than accepting a carry-forward.
Record decisions on any target the business now considers unachievable - either invest or formally change the RTO with the business owner's agreement.
Minute the decisions with owners and dates.
checklist.done: quarterly forum minutes show coverage, results, defect ageing and an owned decision on every unachievable target.

checklist.step: Feed the test results into the Rule 3120 supervisory controls report
actions: Extract the summary of test results - systems tested, pass and fail counts, RTO and RPO performance, open severity one defects - into the report section on testing and verification.
Add the amended or additional procedures arising from the tests, as Rule 3120(a)(2) contemplates, naming the WSP or runbook sections changed.
Cross-reference the BCP annual review conclusion so the two annual obligations reconcile rather than contradict.
Have the Head of Compliance review the section before the report is finalised.
checklist.done: the Rule 3120 report contains a summary of test results and the procedures amended as a consequence, reviewed by Compliance.

checklist.step: Deliver the report to senior management inside the year
actions: Present the Rule 3120 report to senior management at least annually and capture the presentation date, the attendees and the acceptance.
Table the open severity one defects explicitly rather than in an appendix so acceptance of residual risk is conscious.
Record the decisions and the funding commitments in the minutes and post the report to the board portal.
Confirm the delivery date falls inside the calendar year and file the delivery evidence with the report.
checklist.done: the report is presented and accepted inside the calendar year with attendance, decisions and open severity one defects minuted.

checklist.step: Log coverage and result failures as exceptions
actions: Raise an issue for every system untested in the calendar year, every unremediated RTO or RPO miss and every severity one defect past its retest date.
Assign a root cause (window never agreed, environment unavailable, dependency untestable, vendor non-participation) and an owner at manager level or above.
Set a remediation date inside the first quarter of the following year and require a completed test, not a plan, as closure evidence.
Report the open list to the Compliance Committee and the Chief Information Officer each quarter.
checklist.done: every coverage or result failure has an issue, a root cause, an owner and a completed-test closure requirement.

checklist.step: Retain the test evidence for the year
actions: File per test: the plan, readiness checklist, run log, telemetry captures, business validation results, measured RTO and RPO, defects and retest evidence, under Resilience testing / <year> / <system>.
File the Rule 3120 report, its delivery evidence and the minutes in the same year folder.
Apply the 6-year FINRA Rule 4511 retention label with the first two years readily accessible.
Confirm the archive is searchable by system, scenario, test date and defect number.
checklist.done: the year's test record and the Rule 3120 report are archived, retention-labelled and searchable by system and test date.

testing.step: Build the population of mission critical systems and scheduled tests
actions: Extract the tier one system list from the CMDB as at year end with RTO, RPO and business service owner.
Extract the annual test calendar and the completed test records from the ITSM platform for the calendar year.
Compare the CMDB list to the BCP mission critical appendix and list any system critical in one source and absent from the other.
Sign the population as complete before sampling.
testing.done: the system population is reconciled between the CMDB, the BCP appendix and the test calendar, with differences listed.

testing.step: Reconcile test coverage to the population
actions: Match every tier one system to at least one completed test with a date inside the calendar year.
List every system untested, tested only in a lower environment, or tested with the failure injection skipped.
Compute the coverage percentage and compare to the 100 percent threshold.
Confirm each completed test carries a change record and an approval in the ITSM platform.
testing.done: coverage is quantified against the 100 percent threshold and every untested or degraded test is itemised.

testing.step: Draw the test sample and record the method
actions: Take 100 percent of tests covering customer access to funds and securities and books and records retention.
Take 8 further completed tests by seeded random selection across the year.
Record the seed, population size, selection date and selector so the sample can be redrawn.
Confirm no sampled test was planned, executed or signed off by a member of the test team.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers the customer-access and records tests and is free of self-review.

testing.step: Observe a live test and re-perform the measurement
actions: Attend at least one scheduled test in person or on the bridge and record your own timestamps for injection, detection, restoration and business confirmation.
Pull the same window from Grafana and Splunk SIEM and compare the telemetry to the run log timestamps.
Compute achieved RTO from your own timestamps and compare to the reported figure.
Record any difference between observed and reported timings as an exception.
testing.done: at least one test is independently observed with auditor timestamps reconciled to telemetry and to the reported RTO.

testing.step: Re-perform the RPO evidence check on the sample
actions: For each sampled test, obtain the transaction log evidence for the last committed transaction before failure and the last present after recovery.
Recompute the data loss and compare to the reported RPO result and to the CMDB target.
Where the evidence is a summary statement rather than a log extract, record the result as unevidenced.
Capture the log identifiers into the workpaper.
testing.done: RPO is independently recomputed from transaction log evidence for every sampled test or recorded as unevidenced.

testing.step: Test that business validation actually happened
actions: For each sampled test, obtain the business validation script and the recorded results and confirm a named business person signed them.
Confirm the validation exercised real functions - order placed, VA application taken through principal review, statement produced, retained record retrieved - not just a service health check.
Confirm the RTO stop point was the business confirmation, not the infrastructure restoration.
Record any test declared successful without business validation as a fail.
testing.done: each sampled test is shown to have real, signed business validation ending at a business confirmation stop point.

testing.step: Age the defects and test the retest discipline
actions: Extract all defects raised from resilience tests in the year with severity, raise date, due date, closure date and retest reference.
For every severity one defect, recompute days from fix to retest against the 30 day requirement.
Open 10 closed defects and confirm the closure evidence is a retest result, not a statement of intent.
List every severity one defect closed without a retest as a fail.
testing.done: defect ageing is computed, the 30 day severity one retest rule is recomputed and evidence-free closures are failed.

testing.step: Trace the test results into the Rule 3120 report and its delivery
actions: Take the summary of test results in the Rule 3120 report and reconcile the counts to the underlying test records.
Confirm the report states the amended or additional procedures arising from testing and name them.
Confirm the delivery to senior management is evidenced with a date inside the calendar year, attendance and acceptance.
List any softening between the underlying results and the reported summary as an exception.
testing.done: the reported summary reconciles to the test records and the in-year delivery to senior management is evidenced.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the system, the test date and what failed - coverage, measurement, validation, retest or reporting.
Assign a root cause (window never agreed, environment unavailable, measurement to the wrong stop point, vendor non-participation, reporting softened) and an owner at manager level or above.
Set a remediation date inside the first quarter of the following year and require a completed test or a corrected report as closure evidence.
Carry every open exception into next year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a first-quarter date and a completed-test closure requirement.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the resilience testing assurance
actions: Compare results to the thresholds: 100 percent of mission critical systems tested in year, RTO and RPO met, severity one defects retested within 30 days, Rule 3120 report delivered in year.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper references behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who neither planned nor executed any test, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Compliance Committee, the Chief Information Officer and senior management and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion, the coverage percentage, the RTO and RPO results and the report delivery date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the critical third-party and ICT vendor register for the broker-dealer, including the books-and-records providers, the clearing firm, the annuity issuers and the cloud and market data providers named in the FINRA Rule 4370 business continuity plan

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - FINRA Rule 4370 critical business constituent and BCP obligations, Rule 3120(b) additional content of the supervisory controls report, Rule 4513 records of written customer complaints and Rule 2210(d)(6) and (d)(7) testimonials, recommendations and rankings where a vendor produces or hosts retail communications, read against the rulebook at each annual register review

In-scope processes.value: Continuous maintenance of the vendor register: onboarding due diligence, criticality tiering, contract clause verification, ongoing monitoring of SOC 2 and resilience attestations, concentration and fourth-party mapping, and the outsourcing supervision the firm cannot delegate away under FINRA Regulatory Notice 21-29

In-scope systems.value: Vendor register, tiering and assessment workflow in the GRC platform; contracts in the contract lifecycle management repository; spend and onboarding in Coupa / SAP Ariba; system-to-vendor mapping in the CMDB

Compliance procedure documented.value: Third-Party and ICT Risk Register Procedure - register field standard, criticality tiering rules, required contract clauses, assessment cadence by tier, attestation chase rule, concentration and fourth-party mapping, and the exit and substitutability requirement for tier one vendors

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Risk Officer and the Chief Operating Officer, with the contract clause standard approved by the General Counsel and reviewed annually

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Register reviewed in full annually and refreshed within 30 days of any new engagement, renewal or termination; tier one vendors reassessed annually and tier two every two years; SOC 2 Type II reports obtained within 90 days of each report period end; vendor incidents notified to the firm and logged within the contractual notification window, commonly 24 to 72 hours

Deadline reminders configured.value: Assessment due alerts 60 days before each tier one reassessment date, attestation expiry alerts 30 days before a SOC 2 report goes stale at 12 months plus bridge letter, and contract renewal alerts 120 days before expiry so clause gaps can be renegotiated

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Register versions, due diligence packs, SOC 2 reports and bridge letters, contracts and clause checklists, incident notifications and exit plans retained 6 years under FINRA Rule 4511 and SEA Rule 17a-4, and for the life of the contract plus 6 years for books-and-records providers

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Unregistered vendors found in the spend or CMDB data, overdue assessments, expired attestations, missing contract clauses and tier one vendors with no exit plan are logged with owner, compensating control and disposition

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every tier one vendor accepted with an open gap, every concentration breach and the closure of any register completeness failure

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero unregistered vendors supporting a mission critical service or holding books and records; 100 percent of tier one vendors with a current assessment, a current SOC 2 or equivalent, the required contract clauses and a documented exit plan; any vendor holding books and records without the SEA Rule 17a-4 third-party access undertaking is a reportable failure

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is continuous with an annual full review; the test runs annually on the full register with a semi-annual completeness sweep against spend and CMDB data

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual third-party register test workpaper (completeness reconciliation, tiering re-performance, contract clause checks, attestation currency, concentration analysis, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Register export by tier with assessment date, attestation status, contract clause status, exit plan and BCP linkage, plus the fourth-party map for tier one, producible to a FINRA examiner within 5 business days

checklist.step: Fix the register field standard
actions: Define the mandatory fields per vendor: legal entity, service provided, business owner, contract reference and expiry, annual spend, criticality tier, data classification handled, hosting location, regulated activity supported, BCP critical constituent flag and exit plan reference.
Make every field mandatory in the GRC platform workflow so a record cannot be saved incomplete.

Add the FINRA-specific flags: holds books and records under SEA Rule 17a-4, supports order handling or customer access to funds and securities, produces or hosts retail communications subject to Rule 2210.
Publish the standard to business owners with a 30-day window to complete existing records.
checklist.done: the register enforces every mandatory field including the FINRA-specific flags, and existing records have a completion deadline.

checklist.step: Sweep for vendors the register does not know about
actions: Export all suppliers with spend in the last twelve months from Coupa / SAP Ariba with spend amount, cost centre and requester.
Export all externally hosted or vendor-supported applications from the CMDB with the owning business service.
Join both to the register on legal entity and list every supplier or application with no register record.
Route each unregistered item to the named requester or business owner with a 15 business day deadline to register or confirm the engagement has ended.
checklist.done: spend and CMDB data are reconciled to the register and every unregistered vendor has an owner and a 15-day deadline.

checklist.step: Tier every vendor by criticality
actions: Apply the tiering rules: tier one where failure would stop a mission critical service, where the vendor holds books and records, handles customer funds or securities, or is named a critical business constituent in the BCP.
Apply tier two where failure would degrade but not stop a regulated service, and tier three for the remainder.
Have the business owner and the Business Continuity Manager jointly confirm each tier one designation so the register and the BCP agree.
Record the tiering rationale on each record so the judgement is auditable rather than assumed.
checklist.done: every vendor carries a tier with a written rationale, and tier one agrees with the BCP critical constituent list.

checklist.step: Verify the required contract clauses are actually in the contract
actions: Open each tier one and tier two contract in the contract lifecycle management repository and check the clause checklist: right to audit, regulator access, subcontracting consent, service levels with recovery commitments, incident notification window, data location and return, and termination assistance.
For books-and-records providers, confirm the SEA Rule 17a-4 undertaking - the third party's written undertaking to furnish records to the regulator on request - is signed and on file.
For vendors producing or hosting retail communications, confirm the contract requires firm principal approval before use and preserves the Rule 2210 recordkeeping obligation with the firm.
Log every missing clause with the renewal date so it is renegotiated at the next window, and record the compensating control until then.
checklist.done: each tier one and two contract has a completed clause checklist with the 17a-4 undertaking on file where applicable.

checklist.step: Run the tier one due diligence assessment
actions: Issue the assessment questionnaire covering information security, resilience and recovery capability, financial stability, subcontractors, data location and regulatory standing.
Obtain the current SOC 2 Type II report and, where the report period ended more than three months ago, a bridge letter covering the gap.
Read the SOC 2 exceptions and the complementary user entity controls and record what the firm must do at its end for the vendor controls to work.
Record the assessment outcome, the residual risk rating and the reassessment date on the register record.
checklist.done: each tier one vendor has a completed assessment, a current SOC 2 with bridge letter where needed, and the user entity controls recorded.

checklist.step: Chase and track attestation currency
actions: Run the attestation expiry report monthly listing SOC 2 reports, resilience attestations and insurance certificates going stale in the next 60 days.
Chase the vendor contact in writing, escalating to the business owner at 30 days and to the Vendor Manager at 15 days before expiry.
Where a vendor will not provide a report, record the refusal, the compensating control applied and the Chief Risk Officer decision to continue or exit.
Update the register with the received document and its coverage period.
checklist.done: no tier one attestation lapses without a written chase trail and either a received document or a recorded risk decision.

checklist.step: Map the fourth parties behind each tier one vendor
actions: Ask each tier one vendor for its own critical subcontractors supporting the firm's service, with the function and the hosting location.
Record the fourth parties on the register record and flag where several vendors depend on the same underlying provider - cloud region, market data source, transfer agent platform.
Confirm the contract requires notice before a material subcontractor change and record the notice window.
Report the concentration picture to the Operational Risk Manager for the risk register.
checklist.done: each tier one record names its critical subcontractors and shared dependencies are flagged for concentration analysis.

checklist.step: Analyse concentration and substitutability
actions: Aggregate tier one vendors by service type, hosting region and underlying fourth party and identify where one failure would hit multiple mission critical services.
For each concentration, record whether a substitute exists, the switching lead time and whether the data could actually be moved in that time.
Present concentrations exceeding the appetite threshold to the Chief Risk Officer with the options - dual sourcing, contractual protection, or accepted risk with a stated rationale.
Record the decision and the review date on the risk register.
checklist.done: every concentration above appetite has a substitutability assessment and an owned decision recorded on the risk register.

checklist.step: Hold an exit plan for every tier one vendor
actions: Write an exit plan per tier one vendor covering trigger events, the alternate provider or in-house route, the data extraction format and test, the run-off period and the cost estimate.
Confirm the contract supports the plan - termination assistance period, data return format and deletion certification.
Test the data extraction for at least two tier one vendors each year, including a books-and-records provider, and record the result.
Have the business owner and the Operational Risk Manager sign the plan.
checklist.done: every tier one vendor has a signed exit plan and at least two data extractions are tested each year.

checklist.step: Wire vendor incidents into the register
actions: Log every vendor-caused outage, security incident or data event against the vendor register record with the start time, the notification time and the customer impact.
Compare the vendor notification time to the contractual window, commonly 24 to 72 hours, and record every breach of it.
Assess each incident for Rule 4530 reportability and for customer notification obligations with Regulatory Counsel.
Feed the incident history into the next assessment so a poor record changes the risk rating rather than sitting in a separate log.
checklist.done: every vendor incident is logged against the vendor record, tested against the notification window and assessed for reportability.

checklist.step: Reconcile the register to the BCP and the Rule 3120 report
actions: Compare the register tier one list to the BCP critical business constituent appendix and resolve every difference in writing.
Confirm each tier one vendor's recovery commitment in the register matches the recovery assumption in the BCP.
Supply the vendor risk summary - tier one count, overdue assessments, open incidents, concentration decisions - to the author of the annual Rule 3120 supervisory controls report.
Record the reconciliation date and the reconciled version numbers of both documents.
checklist.done: the register and the BCP name the same critical vendors with the same recovery commitments, and the summary reaches the Rule 3120 report.

checklist.step: Run the annual full register review
actions: Send each business owner their vendor records for confirmation of service, tier, spend, data handled and continued need, with a 20 business day return window.
Retire records for ended engagements only on evidence of contract termination and data return or deletion certification.
Refresh the register version, record the review date and the owner confirmations, and publish the register export.
Present the review outcome to the Chief Risk Officer with the count of retired, added and re-tiered vendors.
checklist.done: every record is owner-confirmed or evidenced as retired, and a dated register version is published.

checklist.step: Govern the register at the risk committee
actions: Review quarterly: unregistered vendor sweep results, overdue tier one assessments, expired attestations, open clause gaps, concentrations above appetite and vendor incidents.
Decide on every tier one vendor operating with an open gap - accept with a compensating control and a review date, or require exit.
Minute the decisions with owners and dates and post the pack to the board portal.
Escalate to the Board any concentration or books-and-records gap that could affect the firm's ability to meet a regulatory obligation.
checklist.done: quarterly minutes record an owned decision on every open tier one gap and every above-appetite concentration.

checklist.step: Log register failures as exceptions
actions: Raise an issue for every unregistered vendor found in the sweep, overdue assessment, expired attestation, missing contract clause, missing 17a-4 undertaking and tier one vendor with no exit plan.
Assign a root cause (engagement bypassed procurement, owner change, vendor non-response, contract signed without the clause standard) and an owner at manager level or above.
Set a remediation date inside 90 days and require the underlying artifact - the signed undertaking, the received SOC 2, the amended clause - as closure evidence.
Report the open list with age to the risk committee each quarter.
checklist.done: every register failure has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a 90-day date and an artifact-based closure requirement.

checklist.step: Retain the register and its supporting evidence
actions: File each register version, the due diligence packs, SOC 2 reports and bridge letters, clause checklists, exit plans and incident records under Third-party risk / <year>.
Apply the 6-year FINRA Rule 4511 and SEA Rule 17a-4 retention label, and for books-and-records providers retain for the contract life plus 6 years.
Confirm the archive is searchable by vendor legal entity, tier, contract reference and the books-and-records flag.
Confirm superseded register versions remain retrievable so a point-in-time view can be reconstructed for an examiner.
checklist.done: the register and its evidence are retained, searchable by entity and tier, with point-in-time versions retrievable.

testing.step: Build an independent vendor population
actions: Extract all suppliers with spend in the period from Coupa / SAP Ariba, all externally hosted applications from the CMDB and all critical business constituents from the BCP.
Union the three sources into a single population keyed on legal entity and de-duplicate.
Compare the population to the register export and list every vendor present in a source but absent from the register.
Sign the population as complete before sampling.
testing.done: a three-source independent population is built and every unregistered vendor is itemised as a completeness failure.

testing.step: Reconcile the register to the BCP and CMDB criticality views
actions: Match register tier one records to the BCP critical business constituent list and to CMDB tier one application owners.
List every vendor treated as critical in one view and not the others, and read the tiering rationale on the register record.
Confirm every vendor flagged as holding books and records is also flagged in the register and covered in the BCP.
Record the tiering disagreement count in the workpaper.
testing.done: criticality is reconciled across register, BCP and CMDB with every disagreement listed and the rationale read.

testing.step: Draw the vendor sample and record the method
actions: Take 100 percent of tier one vendors and 100 percent of vendors holding books and records or supporting customer access to funds and securities.
Take 15 further vendors by seeded random selection from tiers two and three.
Record the seed, population size, selection date and selector so the sample can be redrawn.
Confirm no sampled vendor relationship is owned by a member of the test team.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers every tier one and books-and-records vendor and is free of self-review.

testing.step: Re-perform the tiering judgement
actions: For each sampled vendor, read the service description and reach your own tier conclusion using the written tiering rules before looking at the recorded tier.
Compare to the register tier and treat any under-tiering as an exception, including where the recorded rationale does not support the tier.
Check whether any vendor was re-tiered downward during the year and read the justification and the approver.
Record both conclusions and the difference in the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled vendor has an independent tier conclusion and every under-tiering or unjustified downgrade is logged.

testing.step: Verify contract clauses and the 17a-4 undertaking
actions: Open the executed contract for each sampled vendor and read the clauses yourself rather than relying on the checklist result.

Confirm right to audit, regulator access, subcontracting consent, incident notification window, data return and termination assistance are present and check the notification window against the register value.
For every books-and-records vendor, locate the signed SEA Rule 17a-4 third-party undertaking and confirm it names the current regulator access route.
Record every missing clause and every undertaking that cannot be produced as a reportable failure.
testing.done: clauses are independently read for every sampled contract and any missing 17a-4 undertaking is reported as a failure.

testing.step: Test assessment and attestation currency
actions: For each sampled vendor, compute days since the last completed assessment against the cadence - annual for tier one, two-yearly for tier two.
Open the SOC 2 Type II report and check the report period end date, the scope, the exceptions noted and whether a bridge letter covers any gap beyond three months.
Confirm the complementary user entity controls named in the report are assigned to a firm owner and are actually operating.
List every overdue assessment, stale attestation and unassigned user entity control.
testing.done: assessment and attestation currency is recomputed per vendor and unassigned complementary user entity controls are listed.

testing.step: Test exit plans and the data extraction claim
actions: For each tier one vendor, read the exit plan and confirm it names a triggering event, an alternate route, a data format, a run-off period and a cost.
Take the two extraction tests performed in the year and confirm the extracted data was actually readable and complete, not just delivered.
Check the contract supports the plan - termination assistance period and data return format - and flag plans that assume rights the contract does not grant.
Record every tier one vendor with no exit plan or an unsupported plan as a fail.
testing.done: each tier one exit plan is checked against the contract and the year's extraction tests are verified as readable and complete.

testing.step: Test vendor incident handling and notification windows
actions: Extract vendor incidents in the period from the ticketing system and reconcile them to the incidents logged against register records.
For each incident, recompute the hours from vendor awareness to firm notification against the contractual window and list every breach.
Confirm each incident carries a Rule 4530 reportability assessment and, where relevant, a customer notification decision cleared by Regulatory Counsel.
Check whether the incident history changed the vendor risk rating at the next assessment.
testing.done: notification timing is recomputed for every incident and each carries a reportability assessment and a rating impact check.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the vendor legal entity, the tier and what was missing - registration, assessment, attestation, clause, undertaking, exit plan or notification.
Assign a root cause (engagement bypassed procurement, owner change, vendor non-response, contract signed outside the clause standard) and an owner at manager level or above.
Set a remediation date inside 90 days and require the underlying artifact as closure evidence, with a compensating control stated for anything longer.
Carry every open exception into next year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a 90-day date, an artifact-based closure and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the third-party register test
actions: Compare results to the thresholds: zero unregistered vendors supporting a mission critical service or holding books and records, 100 percent tier one assessment, attestation, clause and exit plan coverage.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper references behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who owns no vendor relationship in the population, sign the workpaper.
Report to the risk committee, the Chief Risk Officer and the Compliance Committee, and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion, the unregistered vendor count and the tier one coverage percentages.
